children.title: Subproblem-Cost Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes where splitting subproblems, linear solves, or synchronization dominate first-order work.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regime in which a splitting subproblem's factorization can be reused.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every outer iteration solves Hx=r_k with the same nonsingular matrix H. If forming and factoring H costs C_{\mathrm{fac}} and each subsequent solve costs C_{\mathrm{sol}}, then N outer iterations incur C_{\mathrm{fac}}+NC_{\mathrm{sol}} for this subproblem. If changes in penalty, metric, or representation change H each iteration, this reuse generally disappears and the corresponding cost is \sum_{k=1}^N(C_{\mathrm{fac},k}+C_{\mathrm{sol},k}).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed coefficient matrix permits factorization reuse; changing penalties or metrics can force repeated factorization.
assumptions_latex: H is fixed and nonsingular in the amortized regime
Factorization and per-right-hand-side solve costs are counted separately
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_N^{\mathrm{fixed}}=C_{\mathrm{fac}}+NC_{\mathrm{sol}},\qquad C_N^{\mathrm{changing}}=\sum_{k=1}^N(C_{\mathrm{fac},k}+C_{\mathrm{sol},k}).
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Factor Amortization Regime

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer complexity must include the accuracy schedule and conditioning of iterative subproblem evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a splitting method evaluates resolvents inexactly with errors e_k, exact-resolvent convergence theory cannot be invoked merely from a fixed inner tolerance. Summable perturbations, \sum_k\|e_k\|<\infty, are one standard sufficient regime; other algorithms use specified relative-error criteria. Total work is \sum_k q_k, where q_k is the inner work needed to satisfy the selected criterion and may depend on conditioning and requested outer accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact subproblems need a convergence-compatible error schedule, and their inner work belongs in total complexity.
assumptions_latex: Subproblems are evaluated inexactly
e_k denotes the induced operator-evaluation error
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{outer iteration count alone does not bound work};\qquad W_N=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}q_k.

Subproblem-Cost Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating cheap splitting iterations from hidden linear-system or optimization costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An ADMM or resolvent-splitting iteration is a matrix-free first-order LP step only when every required proximal map or resolvent can be evaluated to the prescribed accuracy using the counted primitive operations. If an update instead requires solving a dense system such as \((A^TA+\mu I)x=r\), factoring a changing matrix, or solving a nontrivial auxiliary optimization problem, then an iteration count alone is not a valid bound on matrix–vector products or arithmetic work. The total complexity must include factorization, triangular solves, inner iterations, conditioning, and the accuracy demanded of inexact subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A splitting method ceases to have cheap first-order iterations when its proximal steps hide dense factorizations, linear solves, or iterative subproblems whose costs are omitted.
assumptions_latex: Complexity is measured in arithmetic operations or matrix–vector products
The algorithm invokes proximal maps or resolvents as subproblems
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{total work}=\sum_k\bigl(\text{outer-step cost}_k+\text{subproblem cost}_k\bigr), so an outer iteration bound alone is insufficient.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual guarantee for the canonical unrestarted anchored iteration.

Halpern PDHG Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Halpern anchoring applied to a nonexpansive PDHG fixed-point map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a nonexpansive fixed-point map induced by a stable PDHG splitting in its natural weighted norm, and let \(a\) be an anchor. Initialize \(z^0=a\), choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1)\), and iterate \(z^{k+1}=\alpha_k a+(1-\alpha_k)Tz^k\). A canonical choice is \(\alpha_k=1/(k+2)\). Stop when the fixed-point residual \(\lVert z^k-Tz^k\rVert\), or the corresponding LP primal–dual residual, meets tolerance. Under the Halpern conditions \(\alpha_k\to0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), and suitable regularity of the weights, the iterates converge to the fixed point selected by the anchor.

children.title: Restart Acceleration Effect
children.top_down_role: Complexity and practical-progress changes attributable to restarting Halpern-style iterations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic work bound obtained by composing certified contractions across restart epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let d_s=\operatorname{dist}(a_s,S), where S\ne\varnothing. If epoch s uses m_s operator evaluations and returns a_{s+1} satisfying d_{s+1}\le\rho_s d_s with 0\le\rho_s<1, then d_r\le d_0\prod_{s=0}^{r-1}\rho_s. If m_s\le m and \rho_s\le\rho<1, then d_r\le\rho^r d_0, and at most m\left\lceil\log(d_0/\varepsilon)/\log(1/\rho)\right\rceil operator evaluations suffice to obtain d_r\le\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly contracting restart epochs compose to give geometric progress, with total work equal to the epoch cost times the required number of contractions.
assumptions_latex: S\ne\varnothing

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the PDHG fixed-point map \(T\) satisfies the residual error bound \(\operatorname{dist}(z,\operatorname{Fix}T)\le\kappa\lVert z-Tz\rVert\) throughout the relevant level set. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear restart acceleration fails without a uniform residual error bound or reliable restart certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Restarting a nonexpansive PDHG-type map does not by itself imply a uniform geometric rate. For the one-dimensional family \(T_q(z)=qz\), with \(0<q<1\), the fixed-point set is \(\{0\}\) and \(\lVert z-T_qz\rVert=(1-q)|z|\); thus the smallest residual error-bound constant is \(\kappa_q=1/(1-q)\), which is unbounded as \(q\uparrow1\). Consequently, no fixed epoch length and contraction factor independent of problem conditioning can guarantee uniform linear convergence over this family. Inexact residuals or restarts chosen without a valid certificate can likewise destroy the contraction test required by restart analyses.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unrestricted LP Saddle Gap Can Be Infinite
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary requiring a restricted comparison set for infeasible averaged iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality-constrained LP \(\min\{0:x=0\}\), use \(L(x,y)=yx\). At the candidate \((x,y)=(1,0)\), comparison with \((u,v)=(0,v)\) gives \(L(1,v)-L(0,0)=v\). Hence \(\sup_{v\in\mathbb R}\{L(1,v)-L(0,0)\}=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an equality-infeasible candidate, the unrestricted dual comparison gap can be infinite, so a finite ergodic certificate generally requires a restricted comparison set.
assumptions_latex: L(x,y)=yx
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{v\in\mathbb R}\bigl(L(1,v)-L(0,0)\bigr)=+\infty.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract ergodic bound under a declared telescoping saddle inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If, for every \(z=(u,v)\in Z\), \[\sum_{k=1}^N\lambda_k\bigl(L(x^k,v)-L(u,y^k)\bigr)\le D(z),\] then \[\mathcal G_Z(\bar x^N,\bar y^N)\le\frac{\sup_{z\in Z}D(z)}{\Lambda_N}.\] If \(D(z)=\tfrac12\lVert z^0-z\rVert_M^2\) and \(R_M:=\sup_{z\in Z}\lVert z^0-z\rVert_M<\infty\), then \(\mathcal G_Z(\bar z^N)\le R_M^2/(2\Lambda_N)\). If also \(\lambda_k\ge\underline\lambda>0\), this is at most \(R_M^2/(2N\underline\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A telescoping weighted saddle inequality yields an inverse-cumulative-weight restricted gap and an O(1/N) rate for weights bounded below.
assumptions_latex: L\text{ is convex-concave}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted Ergodic Average and Restricted Saddle Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical objects used by ergodic primal-dual gap bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For weights \(\lambda_k\ge0\) with \(\Lambda_N:=\sum_{k=1}^N\lambda_k>0\), define \(\bar x^N:=\Lambda_N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N\lambda_kx^k\) and \(\bar y^N:=\Lambda_N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N\lambda_ky^k\). For \(Z=U\times V\), define \[\mathcal G_Z(x,y):=\sup_{(u,v)\in Z}\{L(x,v)-L(u,y)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ergodic iterate is a weighted average, and its restricted saddle gap is the worst saddle-inequality violation over a declared comparison set.
assumptions_latex: \lambda_k\ge0
\Lambda_N>0
L\text{ is convex in }x\text{ and concave in }y
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\bar x^N,\bar y^N)=\Lambda_N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N\lambda_k(x^k,y^k),\qquad \mathcal G_Z(x,y)=\sup_{(u,v)\in Z}[L(x,v)-L(u,y)].
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Ergodic Average and Restricted Saddle Gap

assumptions_latex: The saddle problem is \(\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y} L(x,y)\), where \(L\) is convex-concave and has a saddle point \(z^\star=(x^\star,y^\star)\).
PDHG uses positive weights \(\lambda_k\) and satisfies the standard one-step preconditioned descent inequality in a norm \(\|\cdot\|_M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G_Z(\bar z^N)\le \|z^0-z\|_M^2/(2\Lambda_N)\) for the indicated comparison set, hence the ergodic gap is \(O(1/\Lambda_N)\).

notation.meaning: Cumulative weight and weighted ergodic average.
Restricted primal-dual gap over a comparison set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-gap form; bounded comparison sets avoid the infinite unrestricted LP gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\subseteq X\times Y\) be convex and contain \(z^\star\). If the PDHG descent inequality gives, for every \(z=(u,v)\in Z\), \[\sum_{k=1}^N\lambda_k\bigl(L(x^k,v)-L(u,y^k)\bigr)\le \frac12\|z^0-z\|_M^2,\] then convexity-concavity and averaging imply \[\mathcal G_Z(\bar z^N)\le \frac{1}{2\Lambda_N}\sup_{z\in Z}\|z^0-z\|_M^2.\] Thus constant weights bounded away from zero yield an \(O(N^{-1})\) restricted ergodic-gap certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted PDHG averages have restricted primal-dual gap proportional to the inverse cumulative weight, and therefore an O(1/N) gap under constant positive weights.
knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic Gap Regime

children.title: Ergodic Residual Regime
children.top_down_role: Convergence guarantees for feasibility or optimality residuals evaluated on averaged iterates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact behavior of affine LP feasibility residuals under weighted ergodic averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda_k\ge0\), \(\Lambda_N=\sum_{k=1}^N\lambda_k>0\), and \(\bar x^N=\Lambda_N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N\lambda_kx^k\), one has \(A\bar x^N-b=\Lambda_N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N\lambda_k(Ax^k-b)\). If every \(x^k\) lies in a convex set \(C\), then \(\bar x^N\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine feasibility residuals average exactly, and convex side constraints are preserved by the ergodic average.
assumptions_latex: \lambda_k\ge0
\Lambda_N>0
C\text{ is convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_p(\bar x^N)=\Lambda_N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N\lambda_kr_p(x^k),\qquad x^k\in C\ \forall k\Rightarrow\bar x^N\in C.
review_flags: The identity does not provide a norm rate without additional control.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Residual Averaging Identity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility and radial stationarity tests for an averaged equality-form LP iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(x,y)=c^Tx+y^T(Ax-b)+\delta_C(x)\), where \(C\) is closed and convex, and let \((\bar x,\bar y)\in C\times\mathbb R^m\). For \(R_x,R_y>0\), set \[\mathcal R_{R_x,R_y}:=\sup_{\substack{u\in C,\ \lVert u-\bar x\rVert\le R_x\\ \lVert v-\bar y\rVert_*\le R_y}}\{L(\bar x,v)-L(u,\bar y)\}.\] Then \(R_y\lVert A\bar x-b\rVert\le\mathcal R_{R_x,R_y}\). If \(\mathcal D_{R_x}(\bar x):=\{d:\lVert d\rVert=1,\ \bar x+R_xd\in C\}\), then \[\sup_{d\in\mathcal D_{R_x}(\bar x)}-\langle c+A^T\bar y,d\rangle\le\mathcal R_{R_x,R_y}/R_x.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual-ball tests expose equality infeasibility, while feasible radius-length primal directions expose a radial stationarity residual.
assumptions_latex: C\text{ is closed and convex}
\bar x\in C
R_x,R_y>0
\lVert\cdot\rVert_*\text{ is dual to }\lVert\cdot\rVert
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lVert A\bar x-b\rVert\le\mathcal R_{R_x,R_y}/R_y,\qquad r_{\mathrm{rad}}(\bar x,\bar y;R_x)\le\mathcal R_{R_x,R_y}/R_x.

notation.meaning: Unit directions feasible for a full displacement of length R_x.
Supremal stationarity violation over the declared radial directions.

review_flags: This radial residual need not equal the full normal-cone distance when feasible directions cannot be extended to radius R_x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ergodic Residual Rate from a Residual-Exposing Gap Rate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional rate transfer for averaged LP iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathcal R_{R_x,R_y}(\bar z^N)\le C/\Lambda_N\), then \[\lVert A\bar x^N-b\rVert\le\frac{C}{R_y\Lambda_N},\qquad r_{\mathrm{rad}}(\bar x^N,\bar y^N;R_x)\le\frac{C}{R_x\Lambda_N}.\] Hence weights bounded below by a positive constant give \(O(N^{-1})\) averaged feasibility and radial-stationarity residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual-exposing restricted-gap rate transfers to averaged feasibility and radial-stationarity rates after division by the test radii.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal R_{R_x,R_y}(\bar z^N)\le C/\Lambda_N
R_x,R_y>0
\Lambda_N>0

notation.meaning: Radial stationarity residual from the residual-exposing certificate.

review_flags: Conditional rate transfer, not an independent PDHG descent theorem.
knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic Residual Rate from a Residual-Exposing Gap Rate

assumptions_latex: The LP saddle function is \(L(x,y)=c^\top x+y^\top(Ax-b)+\delta_{\mathbb R_+^n}(x)\).
A restricted-gap estimate is available on independently chosen primal and dual balls around the averaged iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Appropriate restricted gaps bound primal feasibility and dual stationarity residuals of the ergodic average.

notation.meaning: Dual stationarity residual relative to the nonnegative orthant.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual certification requires test-set radii; an unrestricted LP gap may be infinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix radii \(R_x,R_y>0\). Testing the saddle inequality at \(\bar z^N\) against \(v\in \bar y^N+R_y\mathbb B\) gives a term \(R_y\|A\bar x^N-b\|\); testing against feasible perturbations \(u\in\mathbb R_+^n\cap(\bar x^N+R_x\mathbb B)\) exposes dual stationarity. Consequently, a restricted-gap certificate \(\mathcal G_Z(\bar z^N)\le\varepsilon_N\) on these test sets yields \[\|r_p(\bar x^N)\|\le \varepsilon_N/R_y,\qquad r_d(\bar x^N,\bar y^N)\le \varepsilon_N/R_x,\] whenever the corresponding maximizing perturbations belong to \(Z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small restricted gap certifies feasibility and stationarity of the averaged LP iterate, with residual bounds scaled by the available primal and dual test radii.
knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic Residual Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the Ergodic Residual Regime container. A source is required for the exact conversion from the restricted saddle gap to the normal-cone stationarity residual, including the geometry of the admissible primal perturbations and the conditions under which the maximizing directions belong to the comparison set.

children.title: Gap–Residual Certification Link
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which gap control yields residual control or residual control supports gap estimates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility Residuals Do Not Control the Objective Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP counterexample to a residual-to-gap implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{x:x\ge0\}\), represented with \(A=0\), \(b=0\), and \(c=1\). The dual slack is \(s=c=1\). For every \(M\ge0\), the primal point \(x=M\) and slack \(s=1\) are exactly feasible and have zero primal and dual feasibility residuals, while their primal-dual objective gap is \(x^Ts=M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact primal and dual feasibility can coexist with an arbitrarily large objective gap, so feasibility residuals cannot replace a gap test.
assumptions_latex: M\ge0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_p=r_d=0\quad\text{while}\quad g=x^Ts=M\to\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Residuals Do Not Control the Objective Gap

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Missing Support Directions Break Gap-to-Residual Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison-set boundary for restricted saddle-gap certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[0,1]\), let \(L(x,y)=-x\), and evaluate at \(x=0\). With the standard convex normal cone, \(\operatorname{dist}(0,-1+N_C(0))=1\). If the primal comparison set is only \(U=\{0\}\), then \[\sup_{u\in U}\{L(0,y)-L(u,y)\}=0.\] Thus a restricted gap can vanish while the stationarity residual is positive when the comparison set omits a residual-exposing feasible direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted gap need not control stationarity if its comparison set omits the feasible direction exposing the stationarity defect.
assumptions_latex: L(x,y)=-x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal G_U(0,y)=0<1=\operatorname{dist}(0,-1+N_C(0)).

notation.meaning: Primal comparison set used by the restricted gap.
Standard convex-analytic normal cone to C at x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint certificate in terms of the exact primal support defect, without an unjustified metric stationarity conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the Cartesian restricted-gap decomposition, if \(\mathcal G_{U\times(y+R_y\mathbb B)}(x,y)\le\varepsilon\), then \[\lVert Ax-b\rVert\le\varepsilon/R_y,\qquad \sup_{u\in U}\langle c+A^Ty,x-u\rangle\le\varepsilon.\] If \(U=C\), the second inequality is an \(\varepsilon\)-variational-inequality certificate for minimizing \((c+A^Ty)^Tu\) over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small Cartesian restricted gap certifies primal feasibility and a primal variational-inequality defect; a metric stationarity bound needs further geometry.
assumptions_latex: x\in U\subseteq C
R_y>0
\mathcal G_{U\times(y+R_y\mathbb B)}(x,y)\le\varepsilon
\varepsilon\ge0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cartesian Restricted-Gap Decomposition for an LP Saddle Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition separating feasibility exposure from primal comparison exposure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex, \(L(x,y)=c^Tx+y^T(Ax-b)+\delta_C(x)\), \(x\in U\subseteq C\), and \(V=y+R_y\mathbb B\) with \(R_y>0\). Setting \(q=c+A^Ty\), the restricted gap satisfies \[\mathcal G_{U\times V}(x,y):=\sup_{u\in U,\,v\in V}\{L(x,v)-L(u,y)\}=R_y\lVert Ax-b\rVert+\sup_{u\in U}\langle q,x-u\rangle.\] Both terms are nonnegative because \(x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a Cartesian comparison set containing the candidate and a dual ball, the LP restricted gap is exactly a scaled feasibility residual plus a nonnegative primal support defect.
assumptions_latex: C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is convex}
x\in U\subseteq C
R_y>0
V=y+R_y\mathbb B
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal G_{U\times V}(x,y)=R_y\lVert Ax-b\rVert+\sup_{u\in U}\langle c+A^Ty,x-u\rangle.

notation.meaning: Stationarity vector before the normal-cone contribution.
Radius of the dual comparison ball.

review_flags: Metric normal-cone residual conversion requires additional geometry.
knowledge_statements.title: Cartesian Restricted-Gap Decomposition for an LP Saddle Function

assumptions_latex: The LP is represented by a convex-concave saddle function \(L\).
The comparison set contains radius-\(R_x\) and radius-\(R_y\) perturbations needed to expose stationarity and feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A single restricted-gap upper bound is a verifiable joint upper bound on scaled primal and dual residuals.

notation.meaning: Restricted saddle gap at a candidate point.
Available primal and dual perturbation radii.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint certificate for an LP saddle formulation with explicitly bounded comparison directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate \(z=(x,y)\), suppose \(Z\) contains the admissible perturbations that attain the support functions of the primal and dual residual directions. Then \[\mathcal G_Z(z)\ge \max\{R_y\|r_p(z)\|,\ R_x r_d(z)\}.\] Hence \(\mathcal G_Z(z)\le\varepsilon\) simultaneously certifies \(\|r_p(z)\|\le\varepsilon/R_y\) and \(r_d(z)\le\varepsilon/R_x\). Combined with an ergodic gap bound \(\mathcal G_Z(\bar z^N)\le C/\Lambda_N\), this gives residual certificates of order \(O(1/\Lambda_N)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The restricted saddle gap dominates scaled feasibility and stationarity residuals, so an ergodic gap rate transfers directly to a joint residual certificate.

children.title: Averaging Interpretation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits of translating averaged-iterate guarantees into last-iterate or pointwise performance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cancellation Separates Averaged and Pointwise Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary example showing that certification of an average cannot be assigned to constituent or last iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let z^k=(-1)^k\in\mathbb R, let G(z)=|z|, and for even N let \bar z^N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N z^k. Then \bar z^N=0 and G(\bar z^N)=0, whereas G(z^k)=1 for every k\le N, including k=N. Thus a vanishing certificate at the average does not imply a corresponding pointwise or last-iterate certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating iterates average to a perfectly certified point even though every individual iterate has certificate value one.
assumptions_latex: N\text{ is even}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G(\bar z^N)=0\quad\text{but}\quad G(z^k)=1\ \forall k\le N.

notation.meaning: Arithmetic average of the first N iterates.

review_flags: The example establishes the logical non-implication under an average-only hypothesis; it is not asserted to be a PDHG trajectory.
knowledge_statements.title: Cancellation Separates Averaged and Pointwise Certificates

assumptions_latex: Only a convexity-based ergodic gap estimate for \(\bar z^N\) is assumed.
No monotonicity, metric subregularity, or pointwise-rate hypothesis is imposed on the individual iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An ergodic certificate cannot in general be reinterpreted as the same certificate for \(z^N\) or for every constituent iterate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates guarantees for averaged iterates from guarantees for the last or individual iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Convexity gives only \[G(\bar z^N)\le \Lambda_N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N\lambda_kG(z^k).\] The reverse inequality is unavailable: cancellation among residual directions or oscillation of saddle iterates may make \(G(\bar z^N)\) small while \(G(z^N)\), or even every \(G(z^k)\), remains larger. Therefore an \(O(1/\Lambda_N)\) certificate proved specifically for \(\bar z^N\) is not a last-iterate or per-iterate certificate unless an additional pointwise argument is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate for the averaged iterate does not automatically certify the last iterate, because averaging may cancel oscillations or residual directions.
knowledge_statements.title: Averaging Interpretation Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate, and the distinction between averaged and pointwise guarantees is mathematically standard. The record nevertheless supplies no citation or explicit standard-field rationale supporting the claimed separation and oscillation phenomenon.

children.title: Last-Iterate Regime
children.top_down_role: Pointwise convergence and complexity behavior of the current primal-dual iterate.

assumptions_latex: PDHG is represented as \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\) in a Hilbert norm induced by \(M\succ0\).
The map \(T\) is averaged and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The last iterates converge to a fixed point in finite dimensions, while a quantitative last-iterate optimality rate requires further regularity.

notation.meaning: Fixed-point set, coinciding with saddle solutions under the formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convergence statement; it does not assert the ergodic gap rate for the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(z^\star\in S\), averagedness makes \((z^k)\) Feje9r monotone up to a strictly positive multiple of \(\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|_M^2\). Hence \[\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|_M\to0,\qquad z^k\to z^\infty\in S\] in finite dimensions. This is a last-iterate convergence regime, but it alone supplies neither an \(O(k^{-1})\) last-iterate saddle-gap bound nor a geometric distance rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an averaged PDHG map, the actual iterates converge to a saddle fixed point in finite dimensions, but no fast last-iterate gap rate follows automatically.
knowledge_statements.title: Last-Iterate Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits the Last-Iterate Regime container, and finite-dimensional convergence of Picard iterates of an averaged map with a nonempty fixed-point set is plausible. The record does not source the representation of PDHG as an averaged map under the stated metric and step conditions. The word "Feje9r" is also corrupted and should be corrected to "Fejer" or "Fejér" when the sourced record is revised.

children.title: Fixed-Point Residual Regime
children.top_down_role: Complexity behavior measured through displacement or residuals of the iteration operator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise displacement-residual complexity for Picard iteration of an averaged map; it does not itself bound solution distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\), where \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged in the \(M\)-norm, \(0<\alpha<1\), and \(S=\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\). With \(R_k:=\|z^k-Tz^k\|_M\), nonexpansiveness gives \(R_{k+1}\le R_k\). Consequently, for every \(N\ge0\), \[R_N\le\sqrt{\frac{\alpha}{(1-\alpha)(N+1)}}\,d_M(z^0,S).\] Thus the prescribed last-index displacement residual is \(O(N^{-1/2})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The displacement residual of an averaged fixed-point iteration is nonincreasing, so square summability yields an O(1/sqrt N) bound at the prescribed last index.
assumptions_latex: z^{k+1}=Tz^k
T\text{ is }\alpha\text{-averaged in }\|\cdot\|_M,\quad0<\alpha<1
S:=\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_{k+1}\le R_k\quad\text{and}\quad R_N\le\sqrt{\frac{\alpha}{(1-\alpha)(N+1)}}d_M(z^0,S)

notation.meaning: Fixed-point displacement residual at iterate k.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Last-Index Fixed-Point Residual Bound

assumptions_latex: The update map \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged in the \(M\)-norm for some \(0<\alpha<1\).
The fixed-point set \(S=\operatorname{Fix}T\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fixed-point residual is square summable and admits an \(O(k^{-1/2})\) best-iterate bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator residual complexity for an averaged PDHG fixed-point map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Averagedness yields, for every \(s\in S\), \[\|Tz-s\|_M^2\le \|z-s\|_M^2-\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}\|z-Tz\|_M^2.\] Summing along \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\) gives \[\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}R(z^k)^2\le \frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha}d_M(z^0,S)^2.\] Consequently \[\min_{0\le k<N}R(z^k)\le \sqrt{\frac{\alpha}{(1-\alpha)N}}\,d_M(z^0,S).\] A last-index version additionally requires residual monotonicity or a sharper pointwise theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an averaged PDHG map, squared fixed-point residuals are summable and the best residual among the first N iterates is O(1/sqrt N).
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Residual Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role correctly describes the Fixed-Point Residual Regime, and the displayed averaged-operator inequality yields the stated best-iterate bound. An authoritative source with a theorem or page locator is still required for the averagedness inequality and its coefficient.

children.title: Residual-to-Iterate Transfer
children.top_down_role: Regularity conditions linking small fixed-point residuals to proximity or progress of the current iterate.

assumptions_latex: The fixed-point set \(S=\operatorname{Fix}T\) is nonempty.
On a set \(U\), the error bound \(d_M(z,S)\le\kappa\|z-Tz\|_M\) holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every residual certificate inside \(U\) transfers to a distance-to-solution certificate with factor \(\kappa\).

notation.meaning: Metric distance to the solution set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer is local when the error bound is local and global only when it holds globally.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any iterate \(z^k\in U\), the computable residual bound \(R(z^k)\le\varepsilon_k\) implies \[d_M(z^k,S)\le\kappa\varepsilon_k.\] Thus a pointwise residual rate \(R(z^k)\le C\rho_k\) transfers to \(d_M(z^k,S)\le\kappa C\rho_k\). Without the error bound, \(R(z^k)\to0\) identifies asymptotic stationarity but supplies no uniform quantitative estimate of the iterate's distance from the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local error bound converts a computable fixed-point residual into distance from the current iterate to the LP solution set.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Iterate Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits Residual-to-Iterate Transfer, and the displayed implication follows directly from the assumed local error bound. No citation or explicit standard-field rationale is supplied for the metric-subregularity interpretation or its application to the PDHG fixed-point residual.

children.title: Pointwise-Certification Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cases where residual decay does not provide comparable last-iterate solution accuracy.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing-Residual Family Without a Uniform Distance Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample family showing that small displacement residuals do not uniformly control optimizer distance when no error-bound modulus is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\eta<1\), let \(T_\eta:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be \(T_\eta x=(1-\eta)x\). Then \(T_\eta\) is averaged, \(\operatorname{Fix}T_\eta=\{0\}\), and at \(x=1\), \[\|x-T_\eta x\|=\eta\to0,\qquad d(x,\operatorname{Fix}T_\eta)=1.\] The required error-bound modulus is at least \(1/\eta\), so no modulus uniform over this family exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family of averaged contractions can have arbitrarily small displacement at a point that remains unit distance from its fixed point; the missing error-bound modulus diverges.
assumptions_latex: T_\eta x=(1-\eta)x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|1-T_\eta1\|=\eta\to0\quad\text{while}\quad d(1,\operatorname{Fix}T_\eta)=1

notation.meaning: Family parameter controlling both contraction strength and residual size.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing-Residual Family Without a Uniform Distance Certificate

assumptions_latex: An ergodic or best-iterate residual estimate is known.
No residual monotonicity, last-iterate theorem, or error bound is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The available estimate does not certify the prescribed last iterate \(z^N\) or its distance to the solution set.

notation.meaning: Distance to the fixed-point solution set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes best-iterate, ergodic, and prescribed-last-iterate certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inequality \[\min_{0\le k<N}R_k\le C N^{-1/2}\] proves only that some indexed iterate has small residual; it does not imply \(R_N\le C N^{-1/2}\). Likewise, a small residual at \(z^N\) does not imply a quantitative bound on \(d_M(z^N,S)\) without metric subregularity or another error bound. Therefore pointwise certification requires both an estimate attached to the selected iterate and, when iterate accuracy is claimed, a residual-to-distance transfer condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A best-iterate or averaged estimate is not a certificate for the prescribed last iterate, and residual size alone need not control solution distance.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise-Certification Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate, and the logical distinctions among best-iterate, prescribed-last-iterate, and residual-to-distance guarantees are precise. The record has no citation or explicit standard-field rationale supporting these nontrivial boundary claims.

children.title: Error-Bound Regime
children.top_down_role: First-order LP behavior under metric error bounds or related residual-growth conditions.

assumptions_latex: The PDHG update is \(z^+=Tz\) and \(S=\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
There are \(\kappa>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(S\) such that \(d_M(z,S)\le\kappa\|z-Tz\|_M\) for every \(z\in U\).

notation.meaning: PDHG fixed-point map and its fixed-point set.
Metric distance induced by the PDHG norm.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-subregularity form of the local error bound used for linear convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The error-bound regime holds on \(U\) precisely when there exists a finite \(\kappa>0\) such that \[d_M(z,S)\le \kappa\|z-Tz\|_M\qquad\text{for all }z\in U.\] For a polyhedral LP saddle system, this condition is commonly obtained from a Hoffman-type bound after relating \(z-Tz\) to the KKT residual. The neighborhood \(U\), norm \(M\), and modulus \(\kappa\) are part of the condition and cannot be suppressed in a quantitative rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regime assumes a local metric error bound: distance to the PDHG fixed-point set is at most a constant times the fixed-point residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Error-Bound Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role exactly fits the Error-Bound Regime container. The metric error bound itself is stated precisely, but the asserted Hoffman-type derivation for polyhedral LP saddle systems requires a source specifying the KKT-residual-to-fixed-point-residual relation and its assumptions.

children.title: Local Linear-Convergence Regime
children.top_down_role: Geometric-rate behavior within neighborhoods where the required regularity remains effective.

assumptions_latex: The map \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged in the \(M\)-norm.
The local error bound with modulus \(\kappa\) holds on a neighborhood \(U\), and all iterates from index \(k_0\) onward lie in \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Distances of last iterates to the solution set contract Q-linearly after \(k_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Q-linear convergence in distance for an averaged fixed-point representation of PDHG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k\ge k_0\), averagedness and the error bound give \[d_M(z^{k+1},S)^2\le d_M(z^k,S)^2-\gamma\|z^k-Tz^k\|_M^2\le \left(1-\frac{\gamma}{\kappa^2}\right)d_M(z^k,S)^2.\] Whenever \(0<\gamma/\kappa^2\le1\), it follows that \[d_M(z^k,S)\le q^{k-k_0}d_M(z^{k_0},S).\] Thus the number of post-entry iterations needed for distance at most \(\varepsilon\) is logarithmic in \(1/\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once iterates enter the error-bound neighborhood, averagedness converts residual descent into geometric contraction of last-iterate distance to the solution set.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Linear-Convergence Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the Local Linear-Convergence Regime. The contraction calculation is plausible under averagedness, neighborhood entry, and the stated error bound, but the exact coefficient and its applicability to the intended PDHG representation are unsupported by any citation.

children.title: Error-Bound Rate Transfer
children.top_down_role: Dependence of local rate factors and entry thresholds on error-bound parameters.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rate-Factor Dependence on the Error-Bound Modulus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative dependence of the post-entry distance-contraction factor on averagedness and the local error-bound modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\gamma=(1-\alpha)/\alpha\), and suppose averagedness and the local error bound yield \(d_M(Tz,S)^2\le(1-\gamma/\kappa^2)d_M(z,S)^2\) in the regularity neighborhood. In the nontrivial case \(0<\gamma/\kappa^2<1\), the contraction factor is \(q(\kappa)=\sqrt{1-\gamma/\kappa^2}\). It is increasing in \(\kappa\), so a weaker error bound gives a slower guaranteed rate. After neighborhood entry, reaching distance \(\varepsilon\) requires at most \(\left\lceil\log(d_M(z^{k_0},S)/\varepsilon)/(-\log q)\right\rceil\) further iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The guaranteed local contraction worsens monotonically with the error-bound modulus, and the resulting post-entry iteration count is logarithmic in the requested accuracy.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ is }\alpha\text{-averaged in the }M\text{-norm}
d_M(z,S)\le\kappa\|z-Tz\|_M\text{ on the active neighborhood}
0<\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha\kappa^2}<1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(\kappa)=\sqrt{1-\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha\kappa^2}}\text{ increases with }\kappa
knowledge_statements.title: Rate-Factor Dependence on the Error-Bound Modulus

assumptions_latex: For \(k\ge k_0\), \(d_M(z^{k+1},S)\le qd_M(z^k,S)\) with \(0<q<1\).
The certificate functional \(C\) satisfies \(C(z)\le L_Cd_M(z,S)\) on the same neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The distance contraction transfers to an R-linear rate for the certificate functional.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers local distance contraction to residual, feasibility, or restricted-gap rates when locally dominated by distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(k\ge k_0\), local domination and Q-linear distance contraction imply \[C(z^k)\le L_Cd_M(z^k,S)\le L_Cq^{k-k_0}d_M(z^{k_0},S).\] Hence \(C(z^k)\) converges R-linearly with factor at most \(q\). In particular, the fixed-point residual obeys such a domination when \(T\) is locally Lipschitz, while LP feasibility, stationarity, or restricted-gap certificates require their own local domination constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric convergence in distance transfers to any locally distance-dominated residual or gap certificate, with the same geometric factor and a changed constant.
knowledge_statements.title: Error-Bound Rate Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role is suitable for Error-Bound Rate Transfer, and the abstract transfer from Q-linear distance convergence to an R-linear certificate rate follows from the stated domination assumption. Sources are needed for the claimed local domination of the fixed-point residual and for any LP feasibility, stationarity, or restricted-gap specialization.

children.title: Neighborhood-Entry Boundary
children.top_down_role: Global phases, initialization effects, and pathological regions preceding the local linear regime.

assumptions_latex: The error bound is known only on \(U:=\{z:d_M(z,S)\le\delta\}\) for some \(\delta>0\).
A global or pre-asymptotic estimate \(d_M(z^k,S)\le B_k\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local linear rate may begin only after an index \(k_0\) for which \(B_{k_0}\le\delta\).

notation.meaning: Certified global upper bound on solution distance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local linear complexity excludes the unquantified pre-entry phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A contraction derived from the error bound is valid only for indices satisfying \(z^k\in U\). If \(B_k\le\delta\), then \(z^k\in U\), so a certified entry index is \[k_0:=\min\{k:B_k\le\delta\}.\] The subsequent estimate is \(d_M(z^N,S)\le q^{N-k_0}B_{k_0}\) for \(N\ge k_0\). Without a bound on \(k_0\), the local geometric rate does not yield a global iteration-complexity bound; it describes only the post-entry phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local linear rate starts only after certified entry into the error-bound neighborhood; without an entry-time bound it is not a global complexity result.
knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood-Entry Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role correctly fits Neighborhood-Entry Boundary, and the statement clearly limits the geometric estimate to the post-entry phase. No source or explicit standard-field rationale is supplied for the local-rate composition and certified-entry formulation.

Controlled Divergence on Infeasible Instances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal-displacement description of PDHG divergence when the primal-dual fixed-point set is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be the averaged fixed-point operator induced by PDHG for a finite-dimensional linear program, in the positive-definite metric associated with step sizes \(\tau,\sigma>0\) satisfying \(\tau\sigma\lVert A\rVert_2^2<1\). Define \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\) and \(v=P_{\overline{\operatorname{ran}(I-T)}}(0)\). If \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\varnothing\), then \(v\ne0\), \(z^{k+1}-z^k\to -v\), and \(z^k/k\to -v\) in that metric. Thus the iterates diverge at an asymptotically linear, certificate-bearing rate rather than remaining bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For infeasible PDHG fixed-point equations, iterates diverge linearly along the minimal-displacement vector, while successive differences converge to that vector.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is the finite-dimensional averaged PDHG operator.
\(\tau\sigma\lVert A\rVert_2^2<1\).
\(\operatorname{Fix}T=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^{k+1}-z^k\to-v\quad\text{and}\quad z^k/k\to-v\ne0.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits the divergence leaf, but no source is supplied for the precise PDHG metric, averagedness, asymptotic displacement limits, or the claim that an empty fixed-point set forces a nonzero minimal-displacement vector. The phrase "certificate-bearing" is also not mathematically specified. These points require an authoritative theorem-level source.

children.title: Primal Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Computable evidence for primal constraint satisfaction, bound compliance, and scaled primal feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute primal-feasibility certificate for equality-form LPs with nonnegative variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal program \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\). For a candidate \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), define \(r_{p,=}(x)=Ax-b\) and \(r_{p,+}(x)=x_-\), where \((x_-)_i=\max\{-x_i,0\}\). Given tolerances \(\varepsilon_=,\varepsilon_+\ge0\), the pair \((r_{p,=}(x),r_{p,+}(x))\) is a directly verifiable primal residual certificate whenever \(\lVert r_{p,=}(x)\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_=\) and \(\lVert r_{p,+}(x)\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_+\). Zero residuals are equivalent to primal feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality violation and the negative part of a candidate vector jointly certify approximate primal feasibility; both vanish exactly at feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(\varepsilon_=,\varepsilon_+\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_=,\quad\lVert x_-\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_+.\)

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

source_witnesses.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning boundary for interpreting a small absolute primal residual geometrically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\eta>0\), let \(A_\eta=[\eta]\), \(b_\eta=\eta\), and \(P_\eta=\{x:A_\eta x=b_\eta,\ x\ge0\}=\{1\}\). At \(x_\eta=0\), \[\|A_\eta x_\eta-b_\eta\|_2=\eta,\qquad \|(x_\eta)_-\|_2=0,\qquad \operatorname{dist}_2(x_\eta,P_\eta)=1.\] Thus no residual-to-distance constant uniform over all problem data exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute residuals can vanish across increasingly ill-scaled instances while distance to feasibility stays fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|(A_\eta x_\eta-b_\eta,(x_\eta)_-)\|_2\to0\) while \(\operatorname{dist}_2(x_\eta,P_\eta)=1\).

notation.meaning: feasible set of the scaled instance

knowledge_statements.title: No Data-Independent Residual-to-Distance Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hoffman Error Bound for Primal Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioned conversion of equality and nonnegativity residuals into distance from the primal feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{u\in\mathbb R^n:Au=b,\ u\ge0\}\ne\varnothing\). There is a finite constant \(H(A)\) such that, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\operatorname{dist}_2(x,P)\le H(A)\bigl(\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\|x_-\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-dependent Hoffman constant converts the combined primal residual into a bound on distance to feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{u:Au=b,\ u\ge0\}\ne\varnothing\).
Euclidean norms are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}_2(x,P)\le H(A)\|(Ax-b,x_-)\|_2\) for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.title: Hoffman Error Bound for Primal Residuals

children.title: Dual Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Computable evidence for dual constraint satisfaction, reduced-cost consistency, and scaled dual feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute dual-feasibility certificate for the dual of an equality-form LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the dual program \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\}\), let \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) be a candidate and define \(r_d(y)=(A^{\mathsf T}y-c)_+\), with the positive part taken componentwise. Given \(\varepsilon_d\ge0\), the vector \(r_d(y)\) is a directly verifiable dual residual certificate when \(\lVert r_d(y)\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_d\). Moreover, \(r_d(y)=0\) if and only if \(y\) is dual feasible; equivalently, \(s=c-A^{\mathsf T}y\) is a nonnegative dual slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive part of the violated dual inequalities certifies approximate dual feasibility and vanishes exactly for a dual-feasible point.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(\varepsilon_d\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert(A^{\mathsf T}y-c)_+\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_d.\)

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

source_witnesses.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Small Dual Residual Need Not Imply Uniformly Small Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a representation-independent residual-to-distance guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\delta>0\), consider the dual inequality \(\delta y\le0\), whose feasible set is \(D=(-\infty,0]\). At \(y=1\), \[\operatorname{dist}(1,D)=1,\qquad \lVert(\delta y)_+\rVert=\delta.\] Thus the residual tends to zero as \(\delta\downarrow0\) while the distance to feasibility remains one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling a dual inequality can make its residual arbitrarily small without moving the candidate closer to feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_d(1)=\delta\to0\) while \(\operatorname{dist}(1,D)=1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Small Dual Residual Need Not Imply Uniformly Small Distance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hoffman Error Bound for the Dual Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry-dependent conversion of inequality violation into distance from dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\}\) be nonempty. For fixed norms, there is a finite Hoffman constant \(H\) for this inequality representation such that \[\operatorname{dist}(y,D)\le H\lVert(A^{\mathsf T}y-c)_+\rVert\qquad\text{for every }y.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A representation- and norm-dependent Hoffman constant converts dual inequality violation into distance from dual feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(D\ne\varnothing\).
The residual and distance norms are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(y,D)\le H\lVert r_d(y)\rVert\).

notation.meaning: Hoffman constant for the fixed inequality representation and norms

knowledge_statements.title: Hoffman Error Bound for the Dual Residual

children.title: Joint Residual Stopping Criteria
children.top_down_role: Combined interpretation, scaling, and tolerance handling for primal and dual residual evidence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact specialization of the joint residual-and-gap stopping interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\}\), zero primal-feasibility residuals, zero dual-feasibility residual, and zero objective gap are equivalent to \[Ax=b,\quad x\ge0,\quad A^{\mathsf T}y\le c,\quad c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y.\] These conditions certify primal and dual optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero primal and dual residuals together with zero objective gap form an exact primal-dual optimality certificate.
assumptions_latex: The primal-dual pair uses the displayed equality-form convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b,\ x\ge0,\ A^{\mathsf T}y\le c,\ c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y\Rightarrow x,y\) are optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Zero Joint Stopping Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of Gap-Only and Feasibility-Only Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of retaining feasibility and objective-optimality components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Objective agreement alone does not certify feasibility: for \(\min\{0:x=1,\ x\ge0\}\), the candidate \(x=0,y=0\) has zero objective gap but is primal infeasible. Conversely, joint primal-dual feasibility does not certify optimality without a gap test: for \[\min\{x_1:x_1+x_2=1,\ x\ge0\},\] whose dual is \(\max\{y:y\le1,\ y\le0\}\), the pair \(x=(1,0)\), \(y=0\) is primal-dual feasible but has gap one and is not primal optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero gap can coexist with infeasibility, while primal-dual feasibility can coexist with a positive gap and suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Gap-only and feasibility-only termination are each invalid as optimality tests.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Gap-Only and Feasibility-Only Termination
Joint Residual Stopping Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined feasibility and objective-gap stopping test for equality-form primal-dual iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For primal-dual candidates \((x,y)\), tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g\ge0\), and the pair \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,x\ge0\}\), \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\}\), stop only if \(\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_p\), \(\lVert x_-\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_p\), \(\lVert(A^{\mathsf T}y-c)_+\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_d\), and \(\lvert c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y\rvert\le\varepsilon_g(1+\lvert c^{\mathsf T}x\rvert+\lvert b^{\mathsf T}y\rvert)\). This criterion jointly controls primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and objective agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Terminate when primal and dual violations are small and the two objective values agree within a specified scaled tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2,\lVert x_-\rVert_2\}\le\varepsilon_p,\quad\lVert(A^{\mathsf T}y-c)_+\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_d,\quad\frac{\lvert c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y\rvert}{1+\lvert c^{\mathsf T}x\rvert+\lvert b^{\mathsf T}y\rvert}\le\varepsilon_g.\)

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

source_witnesses.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the stopping-criteria leaf, and the displayed test is internally coherent. However, the cited general primal-dual framework locator does not establish the exact norm choices, shared primal tolerance, or objective-gap denominator used here. A source with a specific stopping-criterion locator is required before this convention can be relied upon.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary showing that localized zero gap need not imply global optimality or feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any candidate \(z=(x,y)\), choosing the comparison region \(B=\{z\}\) gives \(G_B(z)=0\), because the sole comparison term is \(L(x,y)-L(x,y)=0\). Therefore a zero bounded-region gap need not certify global feasibility or optimality when the region omits relevant competitors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singleton comparison region gives zero localized gap at every candidate, so localized zero gap alone is not a global certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_{\{z\}}(z)=0\) for every \(z\), including candidates lacking a global LP certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Singleton-Region Failure of Global Certification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering and zero-gap interpretation for nested comparison regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(z\in B_1\subseteq B_2\), then \(0\le G_{B_1}(z)\le G_{B_2}(z)\). Moreover, \(G_B(z)=0\) if and only if \[L(x,\widehat y)\le L(\widehat x,y)\qquad\text{for every }(\widehat x,\widehat y)\in B.\] Thus zero bounded-region gap certifies only the saddle inequalities represented inside \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enlarging the comparison region can only increase the localized gap, and zero gap certifies saddle inequalities only against included competitors.
assumptions_latex: \(z\in B_1\subseteq B_2\).
The bounded-region gap convention of this leaf is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_{B_1}(z)\le G_{B_2}(z)\), and \(G_B(z)=0\) is a restricted saddle certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity and Restricted Saddle Certification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable evaluation of the bounded-region gap for a Cartesian comparison region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(B=X_B\times Y_B\) and \(L(x,y)=c^{\mathsf T}x+y^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\), \[G_B(x,y)=c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y+\sigma_{Y_B}(b-Ax)+\sigma_{X_B}(A^{\mathsf T}y-c),\] where \(\sigma_C(v)=\sup_{u\in C}v^{\mathsf T}u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a Cartesian region, the bounded saddle gap is the objective difference plus support functions of the primal and dual residual directions.
assumptions_latex: \(B=X_B\times Y_B\) is nonempty and bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_B=c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y+\sigma_{Y_B}(b-Ax)+\sigma_{X_B}(A^{\mathsf T}y-c)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Product-Region Support-Function Representation
Bounded-Region Primal-Dual Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Localized saddle gap over a bounded comparison region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R_+^n\), \(Y=\mathbb R^m\), and \(L(x,y)=c^{\mathsf T}x+y^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\). For \(z=(x,y)\in X\times Y\) and a nonempty bounded comparison set \(B\subseteq X\times Y\) containing \(z\), define the bounded-region primal-dual gap by \[G_B(z)=\sup_{(\widehat x,\widehat y)\in B}\bigl(L(x,\widehat y)-L(\widehat x,y)\bigr).\] Because \(z\in B\), \(G_B(z)\ge0\). It measures the largest saddle inequality violation visible within \(B\), remaining finite when \(B\) is compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The bounded-region gap is the largest saddle inequality violation against primal-dual comparison points in a bounded set containing the candidate.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subseteq X\times Y\) is nonempty, bounded, and contains \(z\).
\(L\) is the stated bilinear LP Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_B(z)=\sup_{\widehat z\in B}\bigl(L(x,\widehat y)-L(\widehat x,y)\bigr)\ge0.\)

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

source_witnesses.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf and the formula is mathematically coherent, including nonnegativity because the comparison set contains the candidate. The cited general LP primal-dual framework does not specifically support this bounded-region saddle-gap convention; a locator defining the localized gap is needed.

children.title: Normalized Primal-Dual Gaps
children.top_down_role: Gap measures normalized by selected iterate, data, radius, or reference scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Primal-Dual Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Radius-normalized local gap used to compare bounded regions of different sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z=X\times Y\) carry a norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\), let \(z=(x,y)\in Z\), and for \(r>0\) define \(B_r(z)=\{\widehat z\in Z:\lVert\widehat z-z\rVert\le r\}\). With \(G_{B_r(z)}(z)\) the bounded-region gap, define the radius-normalized primal-dual gap by \[\rho_r(z)=\frac{G_{B_r(z)}(z)}{r}.\] The normalization reports saddle violation per unit comparison radius. Its numerical value depends on the selected primal-dual norm, which must therefore accompany the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide the local bounded-region gap by its positive comparison radius to obtain saddle violation per unit radius.
assumptions_latex: \(B_r(z)\) is formed using a specified norm on the primal-dual product space.

notation.meaning: radius-r comparison ball around the candidate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf, but radius-normalized gaps depend on the precise product-space norm, comparison set, and gap orientation. No source is supplied for this exact convention, so its intended mathematical version cannot be confirmed.

children.title: Relative Primal-Dual Gaps
children.top_down_role: Gap measures expressed relative to objective, iterate, or problem-data magnitudes.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Primal-Dual Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-scale-relative gap with an explicit positive denominator floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primal-dual candidate \((x,y)\), let \(g(x,y)\ge0\) be a chosen absolute primal-dual gap and let \(\delta>0\) be a fixed scale floor. Define the relative primal-dual gap by \[g_{\mathrm{rel},\delta}(x,y)=\frac{g(x,y)}{\max\{\delta,\lvert c^{\mathsf T}x\rvert+\lvert b^{\mathsf T}y\rvert\}}.\] A relative-gap tolerance \(g_{\mathrm{rel},\delta}(x,y)\le\varepsilon\) is therefore equivalent to an absolute-gap tolerance scaled by the larger of the objective magnitude and \(\delta\). The floor makes the definition valid near zero objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative gap divides an absolute gap by objective magnitude, protected by a positive floor so zero-valued objectives remain well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_{\mathrm{rel},\delta}(x,y)=g(x,y)/\max\{\delta,\lvert c^{\mathsf T}x\rvert+\lvert b^{\mathsf T}y\rvert\}.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf and the formula is internally valid, but relative-gap denominators vary materially across the literature. No source supports this particular sum-of-objective-magnitudes denominator and positive-floor convention.

children.title: Gap-Scaling Comparison
children.top_down_role: Scale sensitivity, interpretability, and tolerance comparability across normalization conventions.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Scaling Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conversion between two positive scalings of the same absolute gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g\ge0\) be an absolute primal-dual gap and let \(s_1,s_2>0\) be two scaling denominators. Define \(g_1=g/s_1\) and \(g_2=g/s_2\). Then \[g_1=\frac{s_2}{s_1}g_2.\] Consequently, if \(0<\alpha\le s_2/s_1\le\beta\), then \(\alpha g_2\le g_1\le\beta g_2\). Thus two scaled-gap stopping rules are uniformly equivalent precisely on regions where the ratio of their denominators is bounded above and away from zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two scaled gaps differ exactly by the inverse ratio of their denominators and are uniformly comparable only when that ratio is controlled.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_1=(s_2/s_1)g_2\), and \(\alpha g_2\le g_1\le\beta g_2\) when \(\alpha\le s_2/s_1\le\beta\).

children.title: Near-Zero Reference Boundary
children.top_down_role: Instability or ambiguity of normalized and relative gaps when reference quantities are small or vanish.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Path Dependence at a Vanishing Gap and Reference Scale
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonexistence of a continuous extension for an unfloored gap ratio at the all-zero boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(R(g,q)=g/q\) for \(g\ge0\) and \(q>0\). As \(t\downarrow0\), the paths \((g,q)=(t,t)\), \((t^2,t)\), and \((\sqrt t,t)\) all approach \((0,0)\), while \(R\) tends respectively to \(1\), \(0\), and \(+\infty\). Hence the unfloored ratio has no path-independent continuous extension at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If both an absolute gap and its reference scale vanish, their unfloored ratio may tend to zero, a positive constant, or infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) has no continuous extension to \((g,q)=(0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Path Dependence at a Vanishing Gap and Reference Scale
Near-Zero Reference Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of unfloored relative-gap scaling when reference objective values approach zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the unfloored relative gap \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}=g/(\lvert p\rvert+\lvert d\rvert)\), where \(g\ge0\) is an absolute gap and \(p,d\) are reference objective values. At \(p=d=0\), this expression is undefined. More generally, for any fixed \(g>0\) and sequence \((p_k,d_k)\to(0,0)\) with nonzero denominators, \(g/(\lvert p_k\rvert+\lvert d_k\rvert)\to+\infty\). Hence an unfloored relative tolerance is unstable near zero; a positive floor or a simultaneous absolute-gap test is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative-gap scaling without a denominator floor is undefined at zero objectives and arbitrarily large as nonzero reference values approach zero.
assumptions_latex: \((p_k,d_k)\to(0,0)\) with \(\lvert p_k\rvert+\lvert d_k\rvert>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\frac{g}{\lvert p_k\rvert+\lvert d_k\rvert}\to+\infty.\)

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas certificate for infeasibility of equality constraints with nonnegative variables.

source_refs.locator: 6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal feasibility system \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), a primal-infeasibility ray is a vector \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \[A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y<0.\] The existence of such a vector certifies that \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}=\varnothing\). Multiplication by any positive scalar preserves the certificate, so the normalization \(b^{\mathsf T}y=-1\) may be imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector with nonnegative transposed constraint image and negative right-hand-side pairing certifies that the primal system has no nonnegative solution; positive rescaling preserves the certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Infeasibility Rays

source_witnesses.locator: 6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity as well as sufficiency of the Farkas ray for equality constraints with nonnegative variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exactly one of the following systems is feasible: \[Ax=b,\ x\ge0,\qquad\text{or}\qquad A^\top y\ge0,\ b^\top y<0.\] Consequently, \(\{x\ge0:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\) if and only if such a multiplier \(y\) exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonnegative equality system is infeasible exactly when a dual-side multiplier has nonnegative transposed image and strictly negative right-hand-side pairing.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x\ge0:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\iff\exists y:\ A^\top y\ge0,\ b^\top y<0.

knowledge_statements.title: Unboundedness Interpretation of Rays
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional conversion of infeasibility rays into unbounded feasible recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal-dual pair \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\}\), let \(d\ge0\), \(Ad=0\), \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\). If a primal-feasible \(x^0\) exists, then \(x^0+td\) is feasible and its objective tends to \(-\infty\). Likewise, if \(A^{\mathsf T}q\ge0\), \(b^{\mathsf T}q<0\), and a dual-feasible \(y^0\) exists, then \(y^0-tq\) is dual feasible and its objective tends to \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasibility ray becomes an unbounded improving direction for the opposite formulation when that opposite formulation has a feasible starting point.
assumptions_latex: \(x^0\) is primal feasible for the first implication.
\(y^0\) is dual feasible for the second implication.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^{\mathsf T}(x^0+td)\to-\infty\quad\text{and}\quad b^{\mathsf T}(y^0-tq)\to+\infty.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Improving Ray Without a Feasible Base Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of the implication from a negative-cost recession ray alone to primal unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{-x:0x=1,\ x\ge0\}\). The direction \(d=1\) satisfies \(d\ge0\), \(0d=0\), and \((-1)d<0\), but the primal feasible set is empty. Hence the ray certifies infeasibility of the dual constraint \(0y\le-1\), not primal unboundedness.

assumptions_latex: The convention is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,x\ge0\}\) with dual \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\}\).

children.title: Ray-Normalization Boundary
children.top_down_role: Scaling, numerical detection, and near-degenerate issues affecting interpretation of approximate rays.

knowledge_statements.title: Ray-Normalization Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective normalization of Farkas rays for equality-form linear programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider primal feasibility for \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge 0\). A vector \(y\) is a strict primal-infeasibility ray when \(A^{\mathsf T}y\ge 0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\). Every such ray has the unique positive rescaling \(\widehat y=y/(-b^{\mathsf T}y)\) satisfying \(-b^{\mathsf T}\widehat y=1\). The boundary \(b^{\mathsf T}y=0\) cannot be rescaled to this normalization and supplies no strict Farkas contradiction. Thus objective normalization is valid precisely on the open cone of rays having strictly negative pairing with \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Farkas ray can be normalized to objective value one exactly when its pairing with the right-hand side is strictly negative; zero pairing is the boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(A^{\mathsf T}y\ge 0\) is interpreted componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\iff \exists!\,\alpha>0:\ -b^{\mathsf T}(\alpha y)=1\).
