knowledge_statements.title: Infimal-Displacement Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-theoretic status certificate for a fixed-point formulation of a first-order LP method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be the nonexpansive iteration operator representing the chosen primal-dual LP method on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space \(H\). Its infimal-displacement vector is \[v=P_{\overline{\operatorname{ran}(I-T)}}(0).\] The vector \(v\) is a verifiable fixed-point inconsistency certificate through \(\|v\|=\operatorname{dist}(0,\operatorname{ran}(I-T))\). If \(\operatorname{ran}(I-T)\) is closed, then \(v=0\) exactly when \(T\) has a fixed point; a nonzero \(v\), together with the method-specific primal-dual decoder, yields the corresponding normalized LP status ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum-norm displacement of the iteration operator measures fixed-point inconsistency; when the displacement range is closed, it vanishes exactly when a fixed point exists.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is finite-dimensional and \(T:H\to H\) is nonexpansive.
\(\overline{\operatorname{ran}(I-T)}\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
A specified decoder maps displacement components to LP status rays.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|v\|=\operatorname{dist}(0,\operatorname{ran}(I-T))\), and closedness of \(\operatorname{ran}(I-T)\) gives \(v=0\iff\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: metric projection onto a closed convex set C

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-point displacement facts are plausible, but the navigation does not identify the iteration operator or the decoder that turns its displacement components into normalized LP rays. An operator-theory source and a method-specific LP source are required.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterate-Difference Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-iteration approximation of the infimal-displacement certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Generate \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\) and define the difference certificate \(d^k=z^k-z^{k+1}\). For an averaged nonexpansive operator in finite dimensions, the asymptotic displacement theorem gives \[d^k\longrightarrow v=P_{\overline{\operatorname{ran}(I-T)}}(0).\] Hence \(d^k\) is an asymptotically valid approximation of the infimal-displacement certificate. A finite iterate may be reported with error indicator \(\|d^k-d^{k-1}\|\); status is asserted only after the method-specific decoder applied to \(d^k\) satisfies its Farkas inequalities and normalization tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consecutive iterate differences converge to the infimal-displacement vector and become status certificates once their decoded ray passes explicit Farkas and normalization checks.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is finite-dimensional and \(T:H\to H\) is averaged nonexpansive.
\(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\) for an arbitrary \(z^0\in H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^k-z^{k+1}\to P_{\overline{\operatorname{ran}(I-T)}}(0)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The iterate-difference limit is a nontrivial asymptotic theorem requiring an authoritative locator. The finite certificate checks also depend on an unspecified algorithm-specific decoder and tolerances.

children.title: Normalized-Iterate Certificates
children.top_down_role: Infeasibility or recession evidence extracted from normalized individual iterates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-independent verification of a decoded ray from one nonzero iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a nonzero decoded iterate candidate be \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) or \(d\in\mathbb R^n\). Positive normalization preserves homogeneous equalities, inequalities, and strict-sign predicates. Thus \(\widehat y=y/\|y\|\) certifies primal infeasibility exactly when \(A^\top\widehat y\ge0\) and \(b^\top\widehat y<0\); \(\widehat d=d/\|d\|\) certifies dual infeasibility exactly when \(\widehat d\ge0\), \(A\widehat d=0\), and \(c^\top\widehat d<0\). A zero candidate or failure of any predicate yields no exact status certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalization alone never establishes status; the decoded individual iterate must pass every Farkas or recession-ray predicate.
assumptions_latex: A fixed method-specific decoder supplies \(y\) or \(d\).
The decoded candidate is checked in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A^\top\widehat y\ge0,\ b^\top\widehat y<0\Longrightarrow\text{primal infeasibility};\quad \widehat d\ge0,\ A\widehat d=0,\ c^\top\widehat d<0\Longrightarrow\text{dual infeasibility}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Normalized-Iterate Acceptance Test
Normalized-Iterate Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional certificate extracted from linearly diverging primal-dual iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the primal-dual states satisfy \(z^k/k\to-v\) for a nonzero infimal-displacement vector \(v\). Then \(\|z^k\|\to\infty\), and the normalized iterates obey \[\frac{z^k}{\|z^k\|}\longrightarrow-\frac{v}{\|v\|}.\] Consequently, applying the method-specific ray decoder to \(-z^k/\|z^k\|\) produces an asymptotic unit-norm status certificate. A finite normalized iterate certifies infeasibility or unboundedness only when its decoded components independently satisfy the required sign, homogeneous feasibility, and strict-separation tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If iterates diverge linearly along the displacement direction, their unit-normalized directions converge to the normalized status ray; finite candidates still require direct Farkas checks.
assumptions_latex: \(z^k/k\to-v\) in a finite-dimensional normed primal-dual state space.
A fixed decoder specifies the LP ray inequalities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalization conclusion follows from the stated linear-divergence hypothesis, but neither that hypothesis nor the claimed LP-ray decoder is established for the parent method. Method-specific evidence is required.

children.title: Normalized-Average Certificates
children.top_down_role: Infeasibility or recession evidence extracted from normalized ergodic averages.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verification conditions for a weighted-average ray candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w_j\ge0\) with \(\sum_{j=1}^k w_j=1\). If \(A^\top y^j\ge0\) for every \(j\), then \(\bar y=\sum_jw_jy^j\) satisfies \(A^\top\bar y\ge0\) and certifies primal infeasibility when \(b^\top\bar y<0\). If \(d^j\ge0\) and \(Ad^j=0\) for every \(j\), then \(\bar d=\sum_jw_jd^j\) satisfies \(\bar d\ge0\), \(A\bar d=0\) and certifies dual infeasibility when \(c^\top\bar d<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex averaging preserves homogeneous cone and equality predicates, but the averaged ray must still pass its strict separation test.
assumptions_latex: \(w_j\ge0\) and \(\sum_jw_j=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A^\top y^j\ge0\ \forall j\Longrightarrow A^\top\bar y\ge0;\qquad d^j\ge0,\ Ad^j=0\ \forall j\Longrightarrow\bar d\ge0,\ A\bar d=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Ergodic-Ray Verification
Normalized-Average Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional certificate obtained by normalizing Cesàro averages of divergent iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar z^k=k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{k}z^j\). If \(z^k/k\to-v\) with \(v\ne0\), then \[\frac{\bar z^k}{k}\longrightarrow-\frac{v}{2},\qquad \frac{\bar z^k}{\|\bar z^k\|}\longrightarrow-\frac{v}{\|v\|}.\] Thus the normalized average has the same limiting certificate direction as the normalized last iterate. At finite \(k\), its decoded ray is accepted only after direct verification of the relevant homogeneous feasibility, sign, strict-separation, and normalization conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under linear iterate divergence, normalized Cesàro averages approach the same status-ray direction as normalized last iterates, although finite averages must pass direct certificate tests.
assumptions_latex: \(z^k/k\to-v\) in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar z^k/\|\bar z^k\|\to-v/\|v\|\).

notation.meaning: Cesàro average of the first k iterates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Cesàro scaling and limiting direction are correct conditional consequences of the displayed hypothesis. Evidence is still needed that the parent algorithm has this divergence law and that the decoded finite averages constitute the stated LP certificates.

children.title: Iterate–Average Certificate Comparison
children.top_down_role: Differences in stability, detection speed, scaling, and interpretability between the two certificate sources.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of an ergodic average with the constituent iterates for an affine residual under a common normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(z)=Mz-q\), \(\bar z^k=k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^kz^j\), and \(s>0\). For every norm, \[\frac{\|R(\bar z^k)\|}{s}=\frac{\|k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^kR(z^j)\|}{s}\le\frac1k\sum_{j=1}^k\frac{\|R(z^j)\|}{s}.\] This gives no universal ordering between \(\|R(\bar z^k)\|\) and the last-iterate residual \(\|R(z^k)\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An averaged iterate has residual no larger than the mean norm of affine residuals under a common scale, but it need not outperform the last iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(R(z)=Mz-q\) is affine.
The same norm and positive scale \(s\) are used throughout.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|R(\bar z^k)\|/s\le k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^k\|R(z^j)\|/s\), with no general ordering against \(\|R(z^k)\|/s\).

notation.meaning: Cesàro average of the first k iterates

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Residual Averaging Bound
Iterate–Average Certificate Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic comparison under a common nonzero displacement direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(z^k/k\to-v\ne0\) and \(\bar z^k=k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{k}z^j\), then the last iterate and its Cesàro average have respective first-order growth \[z^k=-kv+o(k),\qquad \bar z^k=-\frac{k}{2}v+o(k).\] Both unit-normalized sequences converge to \(-v/\|v\|\), but the average has half the leading radial magnitude. Their finite-iteration certificate quality is therefore not ordered by this asymptotic fact: averaging may reduce oscillatory error while also reducing the separating margin before normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Last iterates and averages identify the same limiting ray, but averages grow at half the leading rate and may trade reduced oscillation for a smaller raw margin.
assumptions_latex: \(z^k/k\to-v\) with \(v\ne0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The first-order growth, common normalized direction, and one-half norm ratio follow from the assumptions. The claim about oscillatory error and separating margins is algorithm-specific and unsupported, so the complete record needs a source.

children.title: Normalization-Stability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cases where small norms, oscillation, or finite precision destabilize normalized certificate extraction.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalization-Stability Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning boundary of unit-norm certificate extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonzero vectors \(a,b\) in a normed finite-dimensional inner-product space, radial normalization satisfies \[\left\|\frac{a}{\|a\|}-\frac{b}{\|b\|}\right\|\le \frac{2\|a-b\|}{\min\{\|a\|,\|b\|\}}.\] Hence normalization is Lipschitz on every region \(\|a\|\ge\gamma>0\), with constant at most \(2/\gamma\), but is not continuous at the zero vector and has unbounded conditioning as \(\|a\|\downarrow0\). A normalized iterate or average is therefore stable only when its unnormalized certificate magnitude is separated from zero relative to numerical error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unit normalization is stable away from zero but becomes arbitrarily ill-conditioned as the candidate magnitude approaches zero; a reliable certificate needs a positive signal-to-error margin.
assumptions_latex: \(a\ne0\) and \(b\ne0\).
The norm is induced by an inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|a\|,\|b\|\ge\gamma>0\Rightarrow\|a/\|a\|-b/\|b\|\|\le2\|a-b\|/\gamma\), while normalization has no continuous extension at \(0\).

children.title: Fixed Step-Size Regime
children.top_down_role: Convergence and complexity behavior under predetermined primal-dual step sizes.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Step-Size Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-step primal-dual hybrid-gradient regime for a convex LP saddle formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the saddle problem \(\min_x\max_y f(x)+\langle Ax,y\rangle-g^*(y)\), choose constants \(\tau,\sigma>0\) satisfying \(\tau\sigma\|A\|_2^2<1\), initialize \(x^0,y^0\) and \(\bar x^0=x^0\), and iterate \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y^k+\sigma A\bar x^k),\quad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x^k-\tau A^{\mathsf T}y^{k+1}),\quad \bar x^{k+1}=2x^{k+1}-x^k.\] Stop when the prescribed primal, dual, gap, or status-certificate residual tolerance is met; otherwise return the latest state after the iteration budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-step PDHG uses constant primal and dual steps whose product is below the operator-norm stability threshold, and stops when explicit solution or status residuals pass.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex polyhedral functions encoding the LP.
\(A\) is a finite-dimensional linear operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed updates define the fixed step-size regime and preserve a positive-definite primal-dual energy metric.

notation.meaning: constant primal and dual step sizes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record selects a particular extrapolated PDHG variant even though the navigation names no exact method. Its update order, strict step condition, energy metric, and stopping rules require a method-specific citation.

children.title: Adaptive Step-Size Regime
children.top_down_role: Convergence and computational behavior under data-driven or residual-driven step-size changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Step-Size Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient safeguards for variable-step primal-dual splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replace the fixed steps by positive sequences \((\tau_k,\sigma_k)\). A safeguarded adaptive regime requires constants \(\delta>0\) and \(0<m\le M<\infty\) such that \[\tau_k\sigma_k\|A\|_2^2\le1-\delta,\qquad m\le\tau_k,\sigma_k\le M,\] and finite cumulative relative metric variation, \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\left(\left|\frac{\tau_{k+1}}{\tau_k}-1\right|+\left|\frac{\sigma_{k+1}}{\sigma_k}-1\right|\right)<\infty.\] Under the standard solvability assumptions for variable-metric primal-dual splitting, these conditions prevent persistent metric oscillation and retain convergence while permitting residual-based step adjustment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive primal and dual steps remain convergent when uniformly bounded, safely below the coupling limit, and changed by a summable total relative amount.
assumptions_latex: The underlying saddle problem has a solution.
Each iteration uses the same variable-step primal-dual splitting map.
The displayed uniform and summable-variation safeguards hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The variable metrics remain uniformly coercive and asymptotically stable, providing a sufficient regime for convergence of the adaptive iteration.

notation.meaning: adaptive primal and dual step sizes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed safeguards are plausible variable-metric conditions, but sufficiency depends on the precise primal-dual splitting map and metric theorem. Neither the adaptive update rule nor an authoritative convergence result is cited.

children.title: Step-Size Adaptation Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Robustness, tuning burden, overhead, and guarantee differences between fixed and adaptive regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Step-Size Adaptation Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling invariance and metric-balance tradeoff in primal-dual steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For primal and dual steps \(\tau,\sigma>0\), the coupling margin depends on the product \(p=	au\sigma\|A\|_2^2\), whereas the relative scaling of primal and dual motion depends on the ratio \(r=	au/\sigma\). The transformation \[(\tau,\sigma)\mapsto(\rho	au,\sigma/ho),\qquad \rho>0,\] preserves \(p\) but multiplies \(r\) by \(\rho^2\). Thus residual balancing can redistribute progress between primal and dual variables without changing the nominal coupling margin, but aggressive or persistent changes can worsen conditioning and violate convergence safeguards.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reciprocal step changes preserve the stability product while shifting primal-versus-dual scaling; they can balance residuals but may amplify conditioning or adaptation instability.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau,\sigma,\rho>0\).
Stability is controlled by \(\tau\sigma\|A\|_2^2\) for the selected splitting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\rho	au)(\sigma/ho)\|A\|_2^2=\tau\sigma\|A\|_2^2\) and \((\rho	au)/(\sigma/ho)=\rho^2(\tau/\sigma)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product and ratio identities are correct. The interpretation as a stability margin and the claims about residual balancing, conditioning, and persistent adaptation depend on the selected splitting method and need supporting evidence.

children.title: Stability-Limit Boundary
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity to aggressive choices, inaccurate norm estimates, or unstable adaptation.

knowledge_statements.title: Stability-Limit Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definiteness boundary for coupled primal-dual step sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar steps, the standard primal-dual energy matrix is \[M=\begin{pmatrix}\tau^{-1}I&-A^{\mathsf T}\\-A&\sigma^{-1}I\end{pmatrix}.\] By the Schur-complement criterion, \(M\) is positive definite whenever \(\tau\sigma\|A\|_2^2<1\). At \(\tau\sigma\|A\|_2^2=1\), the metric can become singular along a maximal singular-vector pair of \(A\); above this boundary it is indefinite. Consequently, the usual Fejér-energy argument supplies no uniform stability guarantee at or beyond the limit, even though particular structured instances may still converge at equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal-dual energy metric is positive definite below the coupling threshold, may become singular at equality, and becomes indefinite above it, ending the standard stability guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau,\sigma>0\).
\(A\) is a finite-dimensional linear operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau\sigma\|A\|_2^2<1\Rightarrow M\succ0\); equality permits \(M\succeq0\) singular, and a larger product makes \(M\) indefinite.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Schur-complement characterization is mathematically consistent for the displayed PDHG energy matrix, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. A source is required to establish that this is the metric and stability argument intended by the otherwise generic parent navigation.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Weight Balancing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Balancing primal and dual terms in an ergodic gap bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an ergodic primal-dual gap estimate has the form \[G_N\le\frac{1}{2N}\left(\frac{R_x^2}{\tau}+\frac{R_y^2}{\sigma}\right),\] and the admissible step product \(\tau\sigma=q>0\) is fixed. The right-hand side is minimized by equalizing its two contributions: \[\frac{R_x^2}{\tau}=\frac{R_y^2}{\sigma},\qquad \frac{\tau}{\sigma}=\frac{R_x^2}{R_y^2}.\] Thus primal-dual weighting should reflect the squared ratio of anticipated primal and dual distances, while the step product continues to enforce operator-coupling stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a fixed admissible step product, the standard gap constant is minimized when primal and dual distance contributions are equal, determining the optimal step ratio.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau,\sigma>0\) satisfy \(\tau\sigma=q\).
The displayed ergodic gap estimate holds for the selected method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau/\sigma=R_x^2/R_y^2\) uniquely minimizes \(R_x^2/\tau+R_y^2/\sigma\) subject to \(\tau\sigma=q\).

notation.meaning: ergodic primal-dual gap after N iterations
primal and dual weights or step sizes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constrained minimization and optimal step ratio are correct conditional on the displayed gap estimate. The estimate, distance definitions, and metric convention are method-specific and currently unsupported.

children.title: Diagonal Preconditioning
children.top_down_role: Diagonal primal-dual metric choices for balancing operator scales and coordinate sensitivity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient convergence condition for exact-proximal finite-dimensional PDHG with diagonal primal and dual metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the standard Chambolle–Pock/PDHG iteration with exact proximal subproblems, extrapolation parameter \(\theta=1\), positive diagonal step matrices \(T\) and \(\Sigma\), and saddle function \(f(x)+\langle Ax,y\rangle-g^*(y)\), the strict condition \(\|\Sigma^{1/2}AT^{1/2}\|_2<1\), together with existence of a saddle point, is sufficient for convergence of the iterates to a saddle point in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard diagonally preconditioned PDHG converges when the scaled coupling operator has norm strictly below one.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g^*\) are proper closed convex functions.
A saddle point exists.

Diagonal Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal row and column scaling of a standard-form LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\\), \\(b\in\mathbb R^m\\), \\(c\in\mathbb R^n\\), and positive diagonal matrices \\(R\\) and \\(S\\), replace \\(\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\\) by \\(\min\{(Sc)^\top u:(RAS)u=Rb,\ u\ge0\}\\). Initialize with \\(R=I_m\\) and \\(S=I_n\\), choose their diagonal entries from a prescribed scaling rule, and solve the transformed problem. Return \\(x=Su\\). Since \\(S\\) is positive diagonal, this mapping preserves nonnegativity and gives a bijection between the two feasible sets with equal objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale constraints and variables by positive diagonal matrices, solve the equivalent transformed LP, and map the solution back through the column scaling.

\\(R\succ0\\) and \\(S\succ0\\) are diagonal

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic scalar nonuniqueness of row and column factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \((R,S)\) produces \(B=RAS\), then for every \(\alpha>0\), \((\alpha R,\alpha^{-1}S)\) produces the same \(B\). Thus the individual factors are not identifiable without a normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-sided diagonal factors have reciprocal scalar ambiguity.
assumptions_latex: \(R,S\succ0\) are diagonal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\alpha R)A(\alpha^{-1}S)=RAS\).
knowledge_statements.title: Gauge Nonuniqueness of Two-Sided Equilibration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between Euclidean norm equilibration and prescribed-marginal scaling of the entrywise squared matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=A\circ A\), \(r_i=R_{ii}^2\), and \(s_j=S_{jj}^2\). For \(B=RAS\), the equations \(\|B_{i:}\|_2=\rho_i\) and \(\|B_{:j}\|_2=\sigma_j\) are equivalent to \(\sum_j r_iQ_{ij}s_j=\rho_i^2\) and \(\sum_i r_iQ_{ij}s_j=\sigma_j^2\). Thus Euclidean row-and-column equilibration is prescribed-marginal balancing of \(A\circ A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-norm equilibration is prescribed row- and column-sum balancing of the entrywise squared matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(R,S\) are positive diagonal.
\(\sum_i\rho_i^2=\sum_j\sigma_j^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\| (RAS)_{i:}\|_2=\rho_i,\ \|(RAS)_{:j}\|_2=\sigma_j\iff \operatorname{rowsum}(\operatorname{diag}(r)Q\operatorname{diag}(s))=\rho^2,\ \operatorname{colsum}(\operatorname{diag}(r)Q\operatorname{diag}(s))=\sigma^2.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence of Alternating Equilibration for Full Support
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sinkhorn-type convergence under a simple sufficient support condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume every entry of \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) is nonzero and positive targets satisfy \(\sum_i\rho_i^2=\sum_j\sigma_j^2\). Exact alternating row and column normalization is Sinkhorn scaling of the positive matrix \(A\circ A\). Its row and column norm residuals converge to zero; the balanced squared matrix is unique, while the diagonal factors are unique only up to reciprocal scalar gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With full support and compatible positive targets, alternating row and column norm scaling converges to exact equilibration.
assumptions_latex: \(A_{ij}\neq0\) for every \(i,j\).
\(\rho_i>0\), \(\sigma_j>0\), and \(\sum_i\rho_i^2=\sum_j\sigma_j^2\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary sparse-support counterexample to sufficiency of the no-zero-row-or-column condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For A=I_2, p=(1/2,1/2), and q=(1/3,2/3), every matrix supported on A is diagonal and therefore has identical row and column margin vectors. Hence no positive diagonal scaling attains these compatible positive targets, although A has no zero row or column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An identity support cannot realize unequal row and column margin vectors even though every row and column is nonzero.
assumptions_latex: A=I_2

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite scaling, boundary-only attainability, and incompatible-support regimes for prescribed Euclidean equilibration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q=A\circ A and let p,q>0 have equal total mass. If the transportation polytope with margins (p,q) contains a matrix with support exactly \operatorname{supp}Q, finite positive scaling factors exist and exact alternating normalization converges in scaled-matrix space. If it contains a matrix supported in \operatorname{supp}Q but none with exactly that support, the entropy-projection limit lies on a proper support face and logarithmic scaling factors diverge after removal of support-component gauges. If no matrix supported in \operatorname{supp}Q has margins (p,q), simultaneous marginal residual convergence to zero is impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse equilibration has finite-scaling, boundary-limit, and support-infeasible regimes.

p,q>0 and \mathbf1^Tp=\mathbf1^Tq

Finite positive diagonal R,S satisfying \|(RAS)_{i:}\|_2=\rho_i and \|(RAS)_{:j}\|_2=\sigma_j exist if and only if the transportation polytope with margins (p,q) contains a matrix X whose support is exactly \operatorname{supp}Q.

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Support Criterion for Prescribed Euclidean Equilibration
Matrix Equilibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternating Euclidean row- and column-norm equilibration with compatible target norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have no zero row or column, choose \(\tau>0\) and target norms \(\rho,\sigma>0\) satisfying \(m\rho^2=n\sigma^2\), and initialize \(R=I_m\), \(S=I_n\). With \(B=RAS\), perform a row sweep \(R_{ii}\leftarrow R_{ii}\rho/\lVert B_{i:}\rVert_2\), recompute \(B\), and then perform a column sweep \(S_{jj}\leftarrow S_{jj}\sigma/\lVert B_{:j}\rVert_2\). Repeat until \(\max_i|\lVert B_{i:}\rVert_2-\rho|\le\tau\) and \(\max_j|\lVert B_{:j}\rVert_2-\sigma|\le\tau\), or until a prescribed iteration limit. Output the positive diagonal matrices \(R,S\) and \(B=RAS\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternately scale rows and columns toward compatible prescribed norms until the tolerance test succeeds or the iteration limit is reached.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has no zero row or column
\(\rho>0\), \(\sigma>0\), and \(m\rho^2=n\sigma^2\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever the stopping test succeeds, \(B=RAS\) satisfies the stated row- and column-norm tolerances.

children.top_down_role: Connections between diagonal algorithmic metrics and equivalent rescaled LP representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner–Equilibration Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between diagonal data scaling and diagonal primal-dual metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the saddle function \\(L(x,y)=c^\top x+y^\top(Ax-b)\\), set \\(x=Su\\) and \\(y=Rv\\), where \\(R,S\\) are positive diagonal. Then \\(L(Su,Rv)=(Sc)^\top u+v^\top(RAS)u-v^\top Rb\\). Consequently, a Euclidean primal-dual first-order step applied to the scaled operator with matrix \\(RAS\\), when mapped back to \\(x,y\\), is the corresponding original-coordinate step in the diagonal primal and dual metrics \\(S^{-2}\\) and \\(R^{-2}\\). Thus choosing diagonal metrics is equivalent, under this change of variables, to equilibrating the rows and columns of the coupling matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal row-column equilibration is a change of variables that converts Euclidean primal-dual steps into original-coordinate steps with diagonal metrics.
assumptions_latex: \\(R\succ0\\) and \\(S\succ0\\) are diagonal
The first-order update is equivariant under invertible linear changes of variables
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Euclidean geometry for \\(RAS\\) corresponds to metrics \\(S^{-2}\\) and \\(R^{-2}\\) for the original saddle problem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The saddle-function substitution is correct, but the metric correspondence depends on the precise primal-dual update. The generic equivariance assumption is insufficiently inspectable without an identified method and authoritative locator.

children.title: Equilibration Effectiveness Boundary
children.top_down_role: Sparse, ill-scaled, or structurally imbalanced regimes where diagonal scaling offers limited improvement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-rank family showing that equal row and column norms do not control spectral conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\rho<1\), let \(A_\rho=\begin{bmatrix}1&\rho\\ \rho&1\end{bmatrix}\). Both rows and columns have norm \(\sqrt{1+\rho^2}\), but the singular values are \(1+\rho\) and \(1-\rho\). Hence \(\kappa_2(A_\rho)=(1+\rho)/(1-\rho)\to\infty\) as \(\rho\uparrow1\), although every \(A_\rho\) is exactly row- and column-equilibrated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-rank matrix with perfectly equal row and column norms can remain arbitrarily ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_\rho\text{ is equilibrated and nonsingular, but }\kappa_2(A_\rho)\to\infty\text{ as }\rho\uparrow1.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Equilibrated but Arbitrarily Ill-Conditioned Matrices

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural limitation of positive diagonal row and column equilibration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive diagonal \(R,S\), \((RAS)_{ij}=0\) if and only if \(A_{ij}=0\). Thus diagonal equilibration preserves the bipartite support graph, the number and placement of nonzeros, every zero row or column, and structural singularity determined solely by that pattern. It cannot by itself reduce sparse-product work attributable to the stored pattern or remove communication induced by a fixed support partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal scaling changes magnitudes but not the sparse pattern or its structural defects.
assumptions_latex: \(R\succ0\) and \(S\succ0\) are diagonal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{supp}(RAS)=\operatorname{supp}(A)\).

notation.meaning: index set of nonzero matrix entries

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Preservation Boundary of Diagonal Scaling
Equilibration Effectiveness Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal equilibration cannot remove structural rank deficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Positive diagonal equilibration preserves rank: for every \\(R\succ0\\) and \\(S\succ0\\), \\(\operatorname{rank}(RAS)=\operatorname{rank}(A)\\). In particular, take \\(A=\mathbf1_m\mathbf1_n^\top\\) with \\(\min\{m,n\}>1\\). Every scaled matrix \\(RAS=(R\mathbf1_m)(S\mathbf1_n)^\top\\) has rank one, hence has a zero singular value and infinite full-space spectral condition number. Row and column norms may nevertheless be made equal. Therefore successful norm equilibration alone cannot certify nonsingularity, a finite condition number, or improved convergence in directions belonging to the null spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equilibration can equalize norms but cannot repair rank deficiency, so it does not by itself guarantee a finite condition number or faster convergence.
assumptions_latex: \\(R\succ0\\) and \\(S\succ0\\) are diagonal
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For rank-deficient \\(A\\), every \\(RAS\\) remains rank deficient; norm equilibration cannot provide a finite full-space condition number.

knowledge_statements.title: Condition-Aware Row Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row scaling selected by a spectral-condition objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonzero \\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\\) and accuracy \\(\eta>0\\), define \\(\kappa_+(B)=\sigma_{\max}(B)/\sigma_{\min}^+(B)\\), where \\(\sigma_{\min}^+\\) is the smallest positive singular value. Select a positive diagonal \\(R=\operatorname{diag}(r)\\), normalized by \\(\prod_{i=1}^m r_i=1\\), such that \\(\kappa_+(RA)\le(1+\eta)\inf_{D\succ0,\,D\text{ diagonal},\,\prod_iD_{ii}=1}\kappa_+(DA)\\). Apply the row-scaled constraints \\((RA)x=Rb\\). Output \\(R\\) together with the attained condition estimate; the normalization removes the irrelevant common scalar factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose normalized positive row weights that approximately minimize the positive-singular-value condition number, then scale both the constraint matrix and right-hand side.
assumptions_latex: The displayed infimum can be approximated to relative factor \\(1+\eta\\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected \\(R\\) is a \\((1+\eta)\\)-approximate condition-optimal normalized row preconditioner.

notation.meaning: condition number restricted to positive singular values

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record states an oracle selection criterion rather than a method for computing the scaling. A source is needed to establish attainability or approximation and an implementable condition-aware row-scaling procedure.

children.title: Condition-Aware Column Preconditioning

knowledge_statements.title: Condition-Aware Column Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column scaling selected by a spectral-condition objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonzero \\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\\) and accuracy \\(\eta>0\\), select a positive diagonal \\(S=\operatorname{diag}(s)\\), normalized by \\(\prod_{j=1}^n s_j=1\\), satisfying \\(\kappa_+(AS)\le(1+\eta)\inf_{D\succ0,\,D\text{ diagonal},\,\prod_jD_{jj}=1}\kappa_+(AD)\\). Introduce the variable \\(u\\) through \\(x=Su\\), and solve the equivalent constraints \\((AS)u=b\\) with objective \\((Sc)^\top u\\). Output \\(S\\) and the attained condition estimate. Positivity of \\(S\\) ensures that \\(x\ge0\\) is equivalent to \\(u\ge0\\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately minimize the matrix condition number over normalized positive column scalings and apply the resulting scaling as an LP variable transformation.
assumptions_latex: The displayed infimum can be approximated to relative factor \\(1+\eta\\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected \\(S\\) is a \\((1+\eta)\\)-approximate condition-optimal normalized column preconditioner and preserves LP equivalence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary necessary support condition for positive-target joint equilibration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If A has a zero row, no finite positive diagonal R,S can give every row of RAS a common positive norm. If A has a zero column, no such scaling can give every column a common positive norm. Thus a zero row or column precludes positive-target joint equilibration and a finite stationary point of the corresponding log-equilibration potential.

The target row and column norms are positive

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex formulation of simultaneous target row-and-column Euclidean-norm balancing, distinct from condition-number minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}, choose \alpha,\beta>0 with m\alpha^2=n\beta^2, and set R=\operatorname{diag}(e^u), S=\operatorname{diag}(e^v). Then \Phi(u,v)=\frac12\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}^2e^{2u_i+2v_j}-\alpha^2\sum_i u_i-\beta^2\sum_j v_j is convex. Every finite stationary point satisfies \|(RAS)_{i:}\|_2=\alpha for all i and \|(RAS)_{:j}\|_2=\beta for all j, and every such equilibration is stationary. The change (u,v)\mapsto(u+t\mathbf1,v-t\mathbf1) leaves RAS and \Phi unchanged.

m\alpha^2=n\beta^2

knowledge_statements.title: Condition-Estimate Reliability Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Performance guarantees require uniformly reliable scaling-condition estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonzero matrix \(B\), define \(\kappa_+(B)=\sigma_{\max}(B)/\sigma_{\min}^+(B)\), where \(\sigma_{\min}^+(B)\) is its smallest positive singular value. Let \(\mathcal D\) be a normalized family of admissible diagonal-scaling pairs and suppose \(\gamma^{-1}\kappa_+(D_1AD_2)\le\widehat\kappa(D_1,D_2)\le\gamma\kappa_+(D_1AD_2)\) for every \((D_1,D_2)\in\mathcal D\). Any \((1+\eta)\)-approximate minimizer of \(\widehat\kappa\) then has true condition number at most \(\gamma^2(1+\eta)\) times the optimum over \(\mathcal D\). Without a uniform estimate, no finite factor follows. For example, with \(A=I_2\), \(M>1\), \(D_1=\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt M,1/\sqrt M)\), and \(D_2=I_2\), the scaling has determinant-one normalization and true condition number \(M\), yet an unrestricted estimator can rank it as optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniformly multiplicative estimator transfers optimization guarantees with a squared reliability loss; without uniform reliability, even normalized scaling can be ranked arbitrarily badly.
assumptions_latex: \(\gamma\ge1\) and \(\eta\ge0\)
The multiplicative estimate holds uniformly on \(\mathcal D\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform reliability yields approximation factor \(\gamma^2(1+\eta)\); without it, the factor can be unbounded.

notation.meaning: condition number formed from the largest and smallest positive singular values
normalized admissible family of scaling pairs

children.title: Scheduled Restart Regimes
children.top_down_role: Predetermined restart timing choices and the complexity settings in which they are used.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tradeoff between a prescribed contraction factor and fixed restart length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(G(z)\ge\mu\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\) and \(G(T_k(w))\le C\operatorname{dist}(w,Z^*)/\sqrt{k}\), fix \(q\in(0,1)\) and choose \(K_q=\lceil(C/(q\mu))^2\rceil\). Then \(G(z_{j+1})\le qG(z_j)\). Consequently, for \(0<\varepsilon<G(z_0)\), at most \(r=\lceil\log(G(z_0)/\varepsilon)/\log(1/q)\rceil\) restarts and \(K_qr\) base iterations suffice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any prescribed contraction factor determines a sufficient fixed period; certificate halving is the case q equals one half.
assumptions_latex: \(G(z)\ge\mu\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\)
\(G(T_k(w))\le C\operatorname{dist}(w,Z^*)/\sqrt{k}\)
\(0<\varepsilon<G(z_0)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G(z_r)\le q^rG(z_0),\qquad N\le K_q\left\lceil\frac{\log(G(z_0)/\varepsilon)}{\log(1/q)}\right\rceil.

notation.meaning: fixed period sufficient for contraction by q

knowledge_statements.title: General Fixed-Contraction Schedule
Scheduled Restart Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-period restart under a known global sharpness constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \\(G(z)\ge0\\) vanish exactly on the solution set \\(Z^*\\), suppose \\(G(z)\ge\mu\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\\), and assume a base method started at \\(w\\) returns \\(T_k(w)\\) satisfying \\(G(T_k(w))\le C\operatorname{dist}(w,Z^*)/\sqrt{k}\\). Choose the fixed period \\(K=\lceil(2C/\mu)^2\rceil\\), initialize \\(z_0\\), and set \\(z_{r+1}=T_K(z_r)\\). Stop at the first restart index with \\(G(z_r)\le\varepsilon\\), returning \\(z_r\\). Each completed restart reduces the gap by at least a factor of \\(1/2\\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When sharpness and base-rate constants are known, restart after a fixed number of iterations; every restart halves the certificate gap.
assumptions_latex: \\(G(z)\ge\mu\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\\) with \\(\mu>0\\)
\\(G(T_k(w))\le C\operatorname{dist}(w,Z^*)/\sqrt{k}\\)
\\(G\\) is computable for stopping
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(G(z_r)\le2^{-r}G(z_0)\\) for the scheduled period \\(K=\lceil(2C/\mu)^2\rceil\\).

notation.meaning: k iterations of the base method

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-period halving calculation is correct under the displayed global sharpness and base-rate assumptions, and algorithm is the proper role. No authoritative restart reference or LP-certificate specialization is supplied.

children.title: Adaptive Restart Regimes
children.top_down_role: Progress-sensitive restart criteria and their applicable first-order LP settings.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total base-iteration overhead of contraction-tested period doubling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(0<\varepsilon<G(z_0)\). Let \(K_*\) be the first tested power of two satisfying \(K_*\ge (2C/\mu)^2\), and let \(r=\lceil\log_2(G(z_0)/\varepsilon)\rceil\). All trials of length \(K_*\) succeed. The failed trials cost \(1+2+\cdots+K_*/2=K_*-1\), and at most \(r\) accepted trials cost \(rK_*\). Thus \(N<(r+1)K_*\), with \(K_*<2\max\{1,(2C/\mu)^2\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric period search costs less than one additional successful-period block, preserving logarithmic accuracy dependence up to constant overhead.
assumptions_latex: \(G(z)\ge\mu\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\) with \(\mu>0\)
\(G(T_k(w))\le C\operatorname{dist}(w,Z^*)/\sqrt{k}\)
Failed trials restart from the same point with twice the period
\(0<\varepsilon<G(z_0)\)

notation.meaning: first tested power-of-two period guaranteed to halve the certificate
total base iterations including rejected trials

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Doubling Work Bound
Adaptive Restart Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Doubling restart periods until an observed gap contraction occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\ge0\) vanish exactly on a nonempty solution set \(Z^*\), suppose \(G(z)\ge\mu\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\) for an unknown \(\mu>0\), and suppose \(G(T_k(w))\le C\operatorname{dist}(w,Z^*)/\sqrt{k}\) with \(C>0\). Initialize \(K=1\) and a restart point \(z\). Compute \(w=T_K(z)\). If \(G(w)\le G(z)/2\), accept by setting \(z\leftarrow w\) and retain \(K\); otherwise discard \(w\), set \(K\leftarrow2K\), and rerun from the same \(z\). Stop when \(G(z)\le\varepsilon\). Once \(K\ge(2C/\mu)^2\), every trial is accepted. Starting from \(K=1\), this threshold is reached after at most \(\lceil\log_2(\max\{1,(2C/\mu)^2\})\rceil\) doublings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Double the trial period until the computable certificate halves, then reuse that period; the exact doubling bound remains valid for every positive ratio C/mu.
assumptions_latex: \(Z^*\ne\varnothing\)
\(G(z)\ge\mu\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\) for an unknown \(\mu>0\)
\(G(T_k(w))\le C\operatorname{dist}(w,Z^*)/\sqrt{k}\) with \(C>0\)
\(G\) can be evaluated at trial endpoints
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted period is reached after at most \(\lceil\log_2(\max\{1,(2C/\mu)^2\})\rceil\) doublings, and every accepted restart halves \(G\).

notation.meaning: k iterations of the base method

children.title: Restart-Regime Selection Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions favoring scheduled or adaptive restart behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart-Regime Selection Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information conditions separating scheduled, adaptive, and unsupported restarts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the stated restart model, a scheduled regime is justified when valid constants \\(C\\) and \\(\mu\\) are known, because its period can be fixed before execution. If \\(\mu\\) is unknown but the certificate \\(G\\) is computable and the bound holds throughout the visited region, the adaptive doubling regime can test contraction. If \\(G\\) is not observable, if it vanishes away from \\(Z^*\\), or if sharpness holds only inside an unverified neighborhood, neither rule certifies contraction before entry into that neighborhood. Thus local sharpness requires a separate neighborhood-entry certificate or a global preliminary phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Known constants support scheduled restarts; observable gaps support adaptation; unobservable or merely local sharpness prevents certified restart selection without an entry test.
assumptions_latex: The base-method rate uses constant \\(C\\)
Sharpness uses constant \\(\mu\\) on its declared region
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certified selection requires either known \\(C/\mu\\) or an observable contraction test, plus verified validity of sharpness along the restart trajectory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The information boundary between scheduled, observable adaptive, and unsupported local regimes is coherent and fits a failure-boundary container, but it lacks an authoritative locator establishing the restart conditions and neighborhood-entry qualification.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric condition underlying restart acceleration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:Z\to\mathbb R_+\) satisfy \(G^{-1}(0)=Z^*\ne\varnothing\). The certificate is \(\mu\)-sharp on \(D\subseteq Z\) when \(G(z)\ge\mu\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\) for every \(z\in D\). Equivalently, \(\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\le HG(z)\) on \(D\), where \(H=1/\mu\). Global sharpness takes \(D=Z\); local sharpness restricts \(D\) to a declared neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sharpness is a residual-to-distance error bound with reciprocal constants and may be global or local.
assumptions_latex: \(G^{-1}(0)=Z^*\ne\varnothing\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G(z)\ge\mu\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\iff\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\le\mu^{-1}G(z)\quad(z\in D).
knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness and Residual Error-Bound Equivalence
Sharpness-Based Acceleration Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear restart complexity derived from sharpness and a sublinear base rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \\(Z^*\ne\varnothing\\), let \\(G(z)\ge\mu\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\\) with \\(\mu>0\\), and suppose \\(k\\) base iterations from \\(w\\) produce \\(T_k(w)\\) satisfying \\(G(T_k(w))\le C\operatorname{dist}(w,Z^*)/\sqrt{k}\\). Restarting every \\(K=\lceil(2C/\mu)^2\rceil\\) iterations gives \\(G(z_r)\le2^{-r}G(z_0)\\). Hence a point with \\(G(z_r)\le\varepsilon\\) is obtained after at most \\(K\lceil\log_2(G(z_0)/\varepsilon)\rceil\\) base iterations. The bound counts first-order iterations and assumes exact evaluation of the restart certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sharpness converts a square-root sublinear base rate into logarithmic accuracy dependence through fixed-period restarts.
assumptions_latex: \\(G(z)\ge\mu\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\\)
\\(G(T_k(w))\le C\operatorname{dist}(w,Z^*)/\sqrt{k}\\)
\\(0<\varepsilon<G(z_0)\\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration bound is \\(\lceil(2C/\mu)^2\rceil\lceil\log_2(G(z_0)/\varepsilon)\rceil\\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logarithmic restart complexity follows from the stated global sharpness and square-root base-rate assumptions, and complexity_bound fits the container. The record has no authoritative locator and remains generic rather than tied to the parent LP certificate system.

children.title: Hoffman Error-Bound Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Acceleration regimes tied to polyhedral distance bounds and feasibility geometry.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hoffman Error Bound for a Linear System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical polyhedral distance bound underlying Hoffman-based restart acceleration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed matrices \(A,E\) and a fixed norm, there exists \(H<\infty\), depending only on \(A,E\) and the norm, such that every nonempty polyhedron \[S=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Ex=d\}\] satisfies \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le H\left\|\begin{pmatrix}(Ax-b)_+\\Ex-d\end{pmatrix}\right\|\qquad\text{for all }x.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to a nonempty linear-system feasible set is globally bounded by a constant times its inequality and equality violations.
assumptions_latex: The coefficient matrices and norm are fixed.
The linear system is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le H\|((Ax-b)_+,Ex-d)\|\quad\forall x.
knowledge_statements.title: Hoffman Error Bound for a Linear System

assumptions_latex: The solution set \(S\) is nonempty.
The residual \(r_H\) satisfies the Hoffman bound \(\operatorname{dist}(z,S)\le H r_H(z)\) for every iterate.
From any start \(z^0\), the base method satisfies \(r_H(z^t)\le C\operatorname{dist}(z^0,S)/t\) for \(t\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restarting every \(T=\lceil 2CH\rceil\) iterations yields \(r_H(z^{kT})\le2^{-k}r_H(z^0)\); hence at most \(T\lceil\log_2(r_H(z^0)/\varepsilon)\rceil\) base iterations suffice for residual at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract restart bound using a global Hoffman inequality and a sublinear residual estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be the nonempty solution set of a linear-programming system, and let \(r_H:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}_+\) vanish exactly on \(S\). Suppose \(\operatorname{dist}(z,S)\le H r_H(z)\), and a base first-order method started at \(z^0\) produces \(z^t\) satisfying \(r_H(z^t)\le C\operatorname{dist}(z^0,S)/t\). Run the method for \(T=\lceil2CH\rceil\) iterations and restart from its output. Then each restart halves \(r_H\), so \[r_H(z^{kT})\le2^{-k}r_H(z^0).\] Consequently, residual accuracy \(r_H\le\varepsilon\) requires at most \(T\lceil\log_2(r_H(z^0)/\varepsilon)\rceil\) base iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Hoffman bound converts a sublinear residual estimate into geometric decrease when the first-order method is restarted after a fixed number of iterations.
knowledge_statements.title: Hoffman Error-Bound Acceleration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional restart calculation is coherent and the complexity-bound kind fits, but no source identifies a first-order LP method satisfying the stated distance-to-residual rate or supports this restart formulation.

children.title: KKT Error-Bound Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Acceleration regimes tied to primal-dual optimality residual geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixes a concrete residual whose zero set is the primal-dual LP solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), define \(s=c-A^\top y\) and \[R(x,y)=\left\|\begin{pmatrix}Ax-b\\(-x)_+\\(-s)_+\\x\circ s\end{pmatrix}\right\|.\] Then \(R(x,y)=0\) exactly when primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementary slackness hold, equivalently when \((x,y,s)\) is primal-dual optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A norm of primal infeasibility, dual-slack violation, and complementarity is zero exactly at primal-dual LP solutions.
assumptions_latex: The LP is in finite-dimensional standard form.
The residual norm is definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R(x,y)=0\iff Ax=b,\ x\ge0,\ s=c-A^\top y\ge0,\ x\circ s=0\iff (x,y,s)\text{ is primal-dual optimal}.
knowledge_statements.title: Standard-Form LP KKT Residual

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual KKT solution set \(Z^*\) is nonempty.
The KKT residual satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\le\kappa R(z)\) in the relevant level set.
The base method satisfies \(R(z^t)\le C\operatorname{dist}(z^0,Z^*)/t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restarts of length \(T=\lceil2C\kappa\rceil\) give \(R(z^{kT})\le2^{-k}R(z^0)\) and iteration complexity \(O(C\kappa\log(R(z^0)/\varepsilon))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local or level-set KKT error bound coupled to a restartable first-order rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z^*\) be the nonempty primal-dual KKT solution set of an LP, and let \(R(z)\ge0\) be a normed residual incorporating primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity. Assume throughout the iterates' level set that \(\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\le\kappa R(z)\). If the base method satisfies \(R(z^t)\le C\operatorname{dist}(z^0,Z^*)/t\), then a run of \(T=\lceil2C\kappa\rceil\) iterations returns \(z^T\) with \(R(z^T)\le R(z^0)/2\). Repeated restarts therefore satisfy \[R(z^{kT})\le2^{-k}R(z^0),\] giving at most \(T\lceil\log_2(R(z^0)/\varepsilon)\rceil\) iterations to reach \(R\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KKT error bound permits fixed-length restarts that turn a sublinear KKT-residual rate into logarithmic dependence on the target tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: KKT Error-Bound Acceleration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional calculation is coherent and the content kind fits, but the normed KKT residual, invariant level set, and base-method rate are algorithm-dependent and uncited.

children.title: Error-Bound Regime Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Overlap, distinctions, and selection boundaries between the two error-bound viewpoints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Sided Residual Domination Transfers Only One Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary for transferring error bounds between Hoffman and KKT residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_1,r_2\ge0\) have common zero set \(S\). If \(r_2(z)\ge a r_1(z)\) on \(U\), where \(a>0\), then \[\operatorname{dist}(z,S)\le H r_1(z)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{dist}(z,S)\le(H/a)r_2(z).\] The converse requires an upper comparison \(r_2\le b r_1\); equality of zero sets alone implies neither quantitative comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-sided residual domination transfers an error bound in only one direction; common zeros alone do not make two acceleration regimes quantitatively interchangeable.
assumptions_latex: Both residuals are evaluated on a common set \(U\).
The stated domination holds uniformly on \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_2\ge ar_1\text{ transfers the }r_1\text{-bound to }r_2\text{ only; two-way transfer requires }ar_1\le r_2\le br_1.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Residual Domination Transfers Only One Direction

assumptions_latex: Both residuals vanish exactly on the same solution set \(Z^*\).
On a common neighborhood \(U\), constants \(a,b>0\) satisfy \(a r_H(z)\le R_K(z)\le b r_H(z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A Hoffman bound with modulus \(H\) implies a KKT bound with modulus \(H/a\), while a KKT bound with modulus \(\kappa\) implies a Hoffman bound with modulus \(b\kappa\) on \(U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility is expressed as local two-sided equivalence of the chosen Hoffman and KKT residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_H\) be a Hoffman-type residual and \(R_K\) a primal-dual KKT residual, both having zero set \(Z^*\). The two acceleration regimes are compatible on \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) when constants \(a,b>0\) exist such that \[a r_H(z)\le R_K(z)\le b r_H(z)\qquad(z\in U).\] Under this condition, \(\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\le H r_H(z)\) implies \(\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\le(H/a)R_K(z)\). Conversely, \(\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\le\kappa R_K(z)\) implies \(\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\le b\kappa r_H(z)\). Thus restart lengths derived from either residual differ only by the equivalence constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hoffman and KKT restart regimes are compatible when their residuals are locally equivalent; each error bound then transfers to the other with scaled constants.
knowledge_statements.title: Error-Bound Regime Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The transfer constants follow correctly from the stated two-sided residual equivalence, and condition is the appropriate kind. A source is still required to establish that the intended Hoffman and KKT residuals actually satisfy this equivalence on a common neighborhood.
